*   **Swatantra Party**: Founded by **C. Rajagopalachari** in 1959. It was a classical liberal party that advocated for free-market policies and opposed the socialist leanings of the time.

*   **Gadar Party**: Founded by **Sohan Singh Bhakna** and **Lala Har Dayal** in 1913. This revolutionary organization aimed to overthrow British rule in India from abroad, primarily based in San Francisco.

*   **Swaraj Party**: Founded by **Motilal Nehru** and **C.R. Das** in 1923. They sought to participate in the legislative councils to obstruct British policies from within the system.

*   **Forward Bloc**: Founded by **Subhas Chandra Bose** in 1939. He established this faction within the Indian National Congress after resigning from the party presidency due to ideological differences with the leadership.

By aligning these founders with their respective parties, you get the sequence: **A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4**. This sequence confirms the correct choice is the final option provided.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-301.q: When the Government of India had decided to appoint a One Man commission of Inquiry to inquire into the circumstances of the disappearance of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. In 1945 __________’s name was recommended by the then Chief Justice of India
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-301.explanation:
The correct answer is **G.D. Khosla**.

In **1970**, the Government of India appointed a **One-Man Commission of Inquiry** to investigate the mystery surrounding the disappearance of **Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose**.

The then **Chief Justice of India, M. Hidayatullah**, recommended the name of **Justice G.D. Khosla** for this task.

Justice Khosla was a retired Chief Justice of the **Punjab High Court**.

The **Khosla Commission** submitted its report in **1974**, concluding that Netaji had died in the plane crash in **Taihoku** (modern-day Taipei) on **August 18, 1945**.

It is important to note that this was the second inquiry into the matter, following the **Shah Nawaz Committee** of 1956. Later, in 1999, the **Mukherjee Commission** was established to further examine the circumstances of his disappearance.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-302.q: The Cabinet Mission plan was “The best plan put up by the British Government under the then circumstances” described by
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-302.explanation:
The correct answer is **Mahatma Gandhi**. Gandhi described the **Cabinet Mission plan** of 1946 as the best plan the British government could offer given the volatile political situation of that time.

* He believed this mission was a sincere effort by the British to transfer power to Indians while maintaining the unity of the country. Even though he had reservations about certain aspects, he saw it as a positive step toward independence.

* Nehru was critical of the grouping system, Rajaji strongly supported the mission's efforts to keep India united, and Jinnah initially accepted it but later withdrew due to disagreements over the interpretation of the grouping clauses.

Related Facts:
* The Cabinet Mission included three members: **Pethick-Lawrence**, **Stafford Cripps**, and **A.V. Alexander**.
* The main objective of the mission was to discuss the framework for the transfer of power and to draft a new constitution for India.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-303.explanation:
The **Kulakalvi Thittam** (Hereditary Education Policy) was introduced by **C. Rajaji** in **1953** during his tenure as the Chief Minister of Madras State.

This policy proposed that students spend half the day at school and the other half learning their traditional family occupation. It faced massive opposition from political leaders, including those within the Congress party, and the public, as it was criticized for reinforcing the **caste-based** social hierarchy.

Due to the intense political backlash and widespread protests led by **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy**, Rajaji eventually resigned from his position.

Following this, **K. Kamaraj** succeeded him as the Chief Minister in 1954. Kamaraj immediately withdrew the controversial scheme to restore normalcy in the educational system.

Therefore, while Kamaraj is the leader most associated with the school expansion and **Mid-day Meal Scheme**, the Kulakalvi Thittam itself was a policy of **C. Rajaji**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-304.q: Who among the following led the Khudai Khidmatgars in the Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-304.explanation:
The correct answer is **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**.

The **Khudai Khidmatgars**, also known as the **"Red Shirts"** (Lal Kurti), was a non-violent movement founded by **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** in the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP).

This organization played a crucial role in the **Civil Disobedience Movement** by mobilizing the Pashtun population against British colonial rule through peaceful resistance and social reform.

**Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** is famously referred to as the **"Frontier Gandhi"** or **Badshah Khan** due to his deep commitment to Gandhian principles of non-violence and his efforts to promote national unity.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:
* **Abul Kalam Azad** was a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress and a scholar, but he did not lead the Khudai Khidmatgars.
* **Imam Sahab** was a close associate of Gandhi in South Africa and later in India, but he is not associated with this specific movement.
* **Kelappan** (K. Kelappan) was a prominent leader from Kerala who led the **Vaikom Satyagraha** and the salt satyagraha in the Malabar region.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-305.q: Who was considered as “The high Priest of Communism” by the British officials?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-305.explanation:
The correct answer is **M.N. Roy**.

**M.N. Roy** (Manabendra Nath Roy) was a revolutionary, radical activist, and political theorist. He played a significant role in the international communist movement during the early 20th century.

Here is why he holds this distinction:

*   He was a founding member of the **Communist Party of India (Tashkent)** in 1920.
*   He became a prominent figure in the **Communist International (Comintern)**, working closely with **Vladimir Lenin** in the Soviet Union.
*   His deep intellectual engagement with Marxist ideology and his active role in organizing revolutionary activities made him a primary target and a significant figure of interest for the **British Intelligence** agencies.

The British colonial administration viewed his global influence and his efforts to organize socialist movements as a direct threat to their rule in India, leading them to label him with the title **"The High Priest of Communism."**

Other options mentioned:

*   **E.M.S. Namboodiripad** was a prominent leader of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) and the first Chief Minister of Kerala, but he gained prominence later in the political landscape.
*   **Jawaharlal Nehru** and **Subhash Chandra Bose** were giants of the Indian National Congress, but they were primarily associated with the mainstream nationalist movement rather than being the primary focus of "communist high priest" labels by British officials.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-306.q: What was the name of the newspaper started by Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-306.explanation:
Jawaharlal Nehru founded the **National Herald** in **1938** to serve as a voice for the Indian independence movement.

The newspaper was established in **Lucknow** with the goal of promoting the ideals of the **Indian National Congress** and supporting the struggle against British colonial rule. It played a significant role in articulating the vision of a free and democratic India.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Philosophy** is a broad academic discipline and was not a newspaper associated with Nehru.
* **Poorna Swaraj** (Complete Independence) was a political goal declared by the Indian National Congress in 1929, rather than a newspaper publication.
* **Vande Mataram** was the name of a newspaper founded by **Bipin Chandra Pal** and later associated with **Aurobindo Ghosh**, which became a powerful tool for the nationalist cause in Bengal.

Nehru served as the chairman of the board of the **National Herald** for many years, ensuring the paper remained a symbol of the fight for **secularism** and **socialism** in the country.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-307.q: Who started the ‘Samaj Samata Sangha’ to propagate the gospel of social equality among untouchables and caste Hindus?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-307.explanation:
The correct answer is **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**.

He founded the **Samaj Samata Sangha** in **1927** with the primary objective of bridging the social gap between the "untouchable" communities and caste Hindus.

The organization aimed to promote social interaction and break the barriers of **caste-based segregation** through activities like community dining and public discussions. It was a key part of his broader movement to establish **social equality** and human dignity for the marginalized.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **C. Rajagopalachari** was a prominent freedom fighter and the first Indian Governor-General, known for his work in the Congress party, but he did not start this specific organization.
* **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** is best known for the **Bhoodan Movement**, which focused on land reform and voluntary land donation rather than the specific social integration platform of the Sangha.
* **E.V.R. Periyar** led the **Self-Respect Movement** in Tamil Nadu. While his ideology strongly overlapped with the goals of social equality and anti-caste sentiment, the Samaj Samata Sangha was an initiative established by Ambedkar in the Bombay Presidency.

**Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** was a prolific reformer who also founded the **Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha** and the **Independent Labour Party** to advance the cause of the depressed classes.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-308.q: Who was the founder of “All India Scheduled Castes Federation”?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-308.explanation:
The correct answer is **B.R. Ambedkar**.

**Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** founded the **All India Scheduled Castes Federation** in **1942**. This political organization was established to advocate for the rights and political representation of the oppressed classes in India.

The federation played a significant role in highlighting the socio-economic issues faced by the **Dalit** community during the final years of the British Raj. It served as a platform to articulate demands for separate political identities and safeguards for the depressed classes.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Babu Jagjivan Ram** was a prominent Dalit leader and served as the Deputy Prime Minister of India, but he was associated with the **Indian National Congress** and founded the **All India Depressed Classes League**.
* **Y.P. Chavan** and **S.B. Chavan** were senior Indian politicians from Maharashtra, but neither was involved in the founding of this specific federation.

**Dr. Ambedkar's** work with the federation eventually paved the way for the formation of the **Republican Party of India** in 1956, shortly after his passing.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-309.q: Who among the following was regarded as “Moksha Guru” by Bal Gangadar Tilak?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-309.explanation:
The correct answer is **Anna Sahib**. **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** held Anna Sahib in high regard, referring to him as his '**Moksha Guru**' or spiritual mentor. This reflects the deep influence that Anna Sahib had on Tilak's personal philosophy and approach to life.

* **M.G. Ranade** was considered by Tilak as his political guru, which is a different aspect of his intellectual life.
* **V.D. Savarkar** was a younger revolutionary who was inspired by Tilak, rather than the other way around.
* **W.C. Banerjee** was a moderate leader of the Indian National Congress, holding political views that were often at odds with Tilak's extremist ideology.

Related Facts:
* Bal Gangadhar Tilak was a prominent nationalist and one of the first advocates of **Swaraj**.
* He is famous for the slogan '**Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it**'.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-310.q:
Which of the pairs given below is/are incorrect?
I) Gopala Krishna Gokhale - G.A. Natesan
II) Vijaya Ragavachari - Lala Lajpat Roi
III) V.O. Chidambaram - Subramaniya Siva
IV) T. Rengachari - V.S. Srinivasa Sastri
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-310.explanation:
The correct answer is **II only**. This question asks you to identify the incorrect pair among the listed political associations and mentorships during the Indian independence movement.

Pair **II** is incorrect because **Vijaya Ragavachari** and **Lala Lajpat Rai** were prominent leaders from different political ideologies and regions, and they were not a pair associated with one another in the context typically discussed in this historical curriculum.

Pairs **I**, **III**, and **IV** represent correct historical associations:
* **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** was a political mentor to **G.A. Natesan**.
* **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai** and **Subramaniya Siva** were close allies in the Swadeshi movement in Tamil Nadu.
* **T. Rengachari** and **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri** were both influential figures in the Indian National Congress and public life.

Related Facts:
* **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai** and **Subramaniya Siva** were both arrested and imprisoned for their speeches in Tuticorin.
* **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** founded the **Servants of India Society** in 1905.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-311.q: Who among the following was considered as the “Father of Indian Uprising”?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-311.explanation:
The correct answer is **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**.

This title was bestowed upon him by the British journalist **Valentine Chirol**. In his book titled *Indian Unrest*, Chirol identified Tilak as the primary force behind the revolutionary activities in India, referring to him as the **"Father of Indian Unrest"** or the "Father of Indian Uprising."

Tilak was a key figure in the Indian independence movement and a member of the **Lal-Bal-Pal** trio. He is famously remembered for his slogan: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it."**

Here is why the other options do not fit:

* **Bipin Chandra Pal** was a radical leader known as one of the "Mighty Trinity" of the extremist movement, but he was not credited with this specific title.
* **C.R. Das** was a prominent lawyer and the founder of the Swaraj Party, working primarily during the non-cooperation movement era.
* **Gopala Krishna Gokhale** was a **moderate** leader and the political mentor of Mahatma Gandhi, advocating for constitutional reforms rather than the confrontational approach associated with the "Father of Indian Unrest."

Tilak's immense influence on the masses and his ability to mobilize people through festivals like **Ganesh Chaturthi** and **Shivaji Jayanti** made him a primary target for British colonial authorities.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-312.q: In 1895, Shivaji Movement was started by
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-312.explanation:
The correct answer is **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**.

In 1895, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** initiated the **Shivaji Festival** to foster a sense of national pride and unity among the Indian people, particularly in the Maharashtra region. He utilized the legacy of the Maratha ruler **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj** as a symbolic figure to inspire resistance against British colonial rule.

By celebrating the virtues and military achievements of Shivaji, Tilak aimed to bridge the gap between different social classes and ignite a revolutionary spirit. This movement served as a powerful tool for mass mobilization during the **Indian Independence Movement**.

Regarding the other options:

* **Dadabhai Naoroji** was known as the **Grand Old Man of India** and was a key figure in the early years of the Indian National Congress, focusing primarily on economic critiques of British rule.
* **Mahatma Gandhi** entered the Indian political scene much later and focused on the principles of **Satyagraha** and **Ahimsa**.
* **Subash Chandra Bose** was a prominent leader of the later phase of the freedom struggle, famous for organizing the **Azad Hind Fauj** to fight for independence.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-313.q: Satyendranath Tagore was the First Indian who was successful in Indian Civil Service examination in the year
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-313.explanation:
**Satyendranath Tagore**, the elder brother of Nobel laureate **Rabindranath Tagore**, achieved a historic milestone for India in the colonial era.

He was the **first Indian** to successfully clear the **Indian Civil Service (ICS)** examination, which was conducted in London at that time.

Here is the breakdown of his achievement:

*   He traveled to England in 1862 to prepare for and appear in the competitive examination.
*   He successfully passed the examination in **1863**.
*   Following his success, he completed his probationary training and was officially inducted into the service in **1864**.

While historical records often note 1863 as the year of his success in the examination, the timeline is often referenced in the context of his appointment and induction. Based on the options provided, **1863** is the accurate year he passed the exam.

His entry into the ICS broke the monopoly of the British in the higher administrative services of the **British Raj**, serving as a significant inspiration for future generations of Indian nationalists and civil servants.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-314.q: Who remarked these words “Tell me what share I am to have in the Swaraj”?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-314.explanation:
The correct answer is **B.R. Ambedkar**.

This famous remark was made by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** during the **Round Table Conferences** in London. He was expressing his deep concern regarding the political and social rights of the **Depressed Classes** within the proposed framework of self-rule or **Swaraj**.

His primary focus was ensuring that freedom from British rule did not merely transfer power to upper-caste elites while continuing the marginalization of the downtrodden. He demanded clear constitutional guarantees and political representation for his people.

* **Sir Syed Ahmed Khan** was a 19th-century reformer focused on Muslim education.
* **Gopala Krishna Gokhale** was a moderate leader and the political mentor of Gandhi.
* **B.G. Tilak** was an extremist leader famously associated with the slogan, "Swaraj is my birthright."

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-315.q: Which of the following is not associated with Gopal Krishna Gokhale?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-315.explanation:
The correct answer is the **'Voice of India'**. This publication was actually founded by **Dadabhai Naoroji** in 1883 to voice Indian grievances to the British public.

**Gopal Krishna Gokhale's** contributions include:

*   **Servants of India Society**: He founded this organization in 1905 to promote social and human development and prepare national missionaries for the service of India.
*   **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha**: Gokhale was closely associated with this organization, which acted as a bridge between the government and the people. He served as its secretary under the mentorship of M.G. Ranade.
*   **Secretary of the INC**: He served as the **Joint Secretary** of the Indian National Congress in 1903 and later presided over the 1905 Benaras session.

Gokhale is widely remembered as the **political guru** of **Mahatma Gandhi**. He was known for his moderate political views and his emphasis on constitutional methods to achieve self-rule.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-316.q: Who was acclaimed as the “Diamond of India”, due to his invaluable services to the Nation?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-316.explanation:
**Gopala Krishna Gokhale** is widely celebrated as the “Diamond of India.” This title was bestowed upon him by none other than **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, who recognized his immense contribution to the Indian freedom struggle and his high moral integrity.

Gokhale was a senior leader of the **Indian National Congress** and is famously remembered as the political guru of **Mahatma Gandhi**.

He founded the **Servants of India Society** in 1905, an organization dedicated to social service, education, and the promotion of national interests. His approach was defined by **moderation**, rational debate, and deep respect for constitutional methods.

Here is why the other options do not fit this specific title:

* **Bala Gangadhar Tilak** was known as the "Lokamanya," meaning beloved leader of the people, due to his radical approach and popularity.
* **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** is famously known as the "Iron Man of India" for his instrumental role in unifying the princely states.
* **Lala Lajpat Rai** is best remembered as the "Punjab Kesari" or the "Lion of Punjab" for his fearless leadership against British colonial rule.

Gokhale’s dedication to the upliftment of the country through peaceful and ethical means remains a cornerstone of India's intellectual political history.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-317.q: Kamaraj was elected as the Chairman of Virudhunagar Municipality in 1941 when he was in
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-317.explanation:
**K. Kamaraj**, the legendary leader and former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, was an active participant in the **Indian Independence Movement**.

In **1941**, while he was imprisoned for his political activities against British rule, he was elected as the **Chairman of the Virudhunagar Municipality**.

He was serving his sentence in **Vellore Jail** at the time of this election.

This event highlights his immense popularity and the trust the people of his hometown had in his leadership, even while he was behind bars.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:
* **Palayamkottai, Virudhunagar, and Madras Jails** were also significant locations where freedom fighters were held during the colonial era, but Kamaraj was specifically detained in **Vellore Jail** during the 1941 municipal election.

Kamaraj's tenure as Chairman from within the jail walls remains a unique milestone in the history of Indian local governance. He later went on to be known as the **"Kingmaker"** of Indian politics and a pioneer of the **Mid-day Meal Scheme** in Tamil Nadu.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-318.q:
Which of the following statement/s about V.O. Chidambaram is/are true?
I) He was disciple of Tilak and the extremists under his leadership took the lead in Madras Presidency
II) He was honest and he never appeared in the court for false cases
III) He bought ships from France and England
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-318.explanation:
The correct answer is **I and II**. **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai**, popularly known as **Kappalottiya Thamizhan**, was a stalwart of the Indian independence movement in Tamil Nadu.

He was a dedicated follower of **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** and firmly believed in the **Extremist** ideology within the Congress. Under his leadership, the Extremist faction gained significant momentum in the **Madras Presidency**.

He was famously known for his unwavering **integrity** and moral standards. He refused to represent clients in cases he knew to be false, cementing his reputation as an honest lawyer.

Regarding the third statement, he famously purchased two ships named **S.S. Gallia** and **S.S. Lawoe** specifically from **France**, not England, making the statement incorrect.

Related Facts:
* He founded the **Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company** in 1906.
* He was imprisoned for his role in the **Tuticorin Coral Mill strike**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-319.q: Which one of the following was not written by V.O. Chidambaram?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-319.explanation:
**V.O. Chidambaram Pillai**, popularly known as **Kappalottiya Thamizhan**, was a renowned freedom fighter and a prolific writer. He made significant contributions to Tamil literature while imprisoned and during his political career.

The correct answer is **Suryodayam**.

Here is why:

*   **Meyarivu** (True Knowledge) and **Meyiaram** (True Virtue) are celebrated works authored by V.O. Chidambaram to promote moral and ethical living among the public.
*   **Padal Thirattu** is a collection of his poems and songs, which reflect his patriotic fervor and philosophical outlook.
*   **Suryodayam** was not written by him. It was a newspaper published by **Thrikkumara Subramania Iyer** in Pondicherry, which played a vital role in the national movement.

V.O. Chidambaram is also famous for his **Autobiography** (Suyasarithai), which provides deep insights into his life, his struggle for Indian independence, and his experience with the **Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company**. His works remain an essential part of Tamil intellectual heritage.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-320.q: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
options: Savitri Bai Phule - Servants of India Society
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-320.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2, **Savitri Bai Phule - Servants of India Society**. This is the incorrectly matched pair because the **Servants of India Society** was founded by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** in 1905, not Savitri Bai Phule.

Here is the breakdown of the other pairs:

* **Dadabhai Naoroji** helped establish the **East India Association** in London in 1866 to present the Indian perspective to the British public. This is a correctly matched pair.

* **Surendranath Banerjee** co-founded the **Indian Association** in 1876, which served as a precursor to the Indian National Congress. This is a correctly matched pair.

* **A.O. Hume** was a retired British civil servant who played a pivotal role in the formation of the **Indian National Congress** in 1885. This is a correctly matched pair.

**Savitri Bai Phule** is renowned for her pioneering work in women's education and social reform, specifically in Maharashtra, but she is not associated with the establishment of the Servants of India Society.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-321.q: __________ was the first Muslim leader to demand for Pakistan in 1933
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-321.explanation:
The correct answer is **Choudhry Rahmat Ali**. Although the provided option index points to Sayyid Ahamed, history identifies **Choudhry Rahmat Ali** as the individual who coined the term "Pakistan" and first formally demanded a separate Muslim state.

In **January 1933**, he published a pamphlet titled **"Now or Never; Are We to Live or Perish Forever?"**. In this document, he proposed the creation of a separate state for Muslims in the northwestern regions of British India.

Here is why the other figures differ:

* **Choudhry Rahmat Ali**: He is credited with conceiving the name **Pakistan** (an acronym representing Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh, and Baluchistan) and advocating for it while studying at Cambridge.
* **Muhammed Ali Jinnah**: While he later became the primary political leader of the movement and the founder of Pakistan, he did not demand the state in 1933. He formally adopted the demand for Pakistan only during the **Lahore Session** of the Muslim League in **1940**.
* **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**: He was a staunch advocate of **Indian nationalism** and a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress who consistently opposed the partition of India.
* **Sayyid Ahmed Khan**: He was a 19th-century educationalist and reformer who founded the **Aligarh Movement**. While he promoted modern education for Muslims, he focused on social and educational upliftment rather than the political demand for Pakistan.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-322.q: In which of the following jails, the book “Discovery of India” was written by Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-322.explanation:
The correct answer is **Ahmadnagar Fort Jail**.

Jawaharlal Nehru wrote the famous book **"Discovery of India"** during his imprisonment in the **Ahmadnagar Fort Jail** between **1942 and 1946**.

He was held there along with other members of the **Congress Working Committee** following the launch of the **Quit India Movement**. The book serves as a profound exploration of Indian history, philosophy, and culture, written while Nehru was in isolation from the political world.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Yervada Jail**: This is where Mahatma Gandhi and Nehru were imprisoned at various times, but it is specifically famous for the **Poona Pact** signed between Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar.
* **Alipur Central Jail**: This jail is historically significant for the **Alipore Bomb Case** involving Aurobindo Ghosh and other revolutionaries.
* **Deoli Camp Jail**: This facility was primarily used to detain political prisoners and revolutionaries during the British colonial period but was not the site where this specific literary work was authored.

Nehru wrote "Discovery of India" in just five months, utilizing the time in confinement to document the intellectual heritage of his nation.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-323.q:
Which of the following statements are true about V.O.C.?
i) He founded Chennai Vivasaya - Kaitholil Sangam Ltd.
ii) He resigned from the Post of the President of Congress
iii) He was the leader of Chennai Jana Sangam
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-323.explanation:
**V.O. Chidambaranar** (V.O.C.), also known as **Kappalottiya Thamizhan**, was a pivotal figure in the Indian freedom struggle.

Statement (i) is **true**. V.O.C. played a key role in the formation of the **Chennai Vivasaya - Kaitholil Sangam Ltd.** (Madras Agricultural and Industrial Society) in 1906, aimed at promoting indigenous industries.

Statement (iii) is **true**. V.O.C. was a prominent leader of the **Chennai Jana Sangam**, an organization established to support the **Swadeshi movement** and promote nationalist ideas among the public.

Statement (ii) is **false**. While V.O.C. was deeply involved in the activities of the **Indian National Congress**, he did not hold the position of President of the Congress. His political work was primarily focused on mobilizing the labor force and promoting **Swadeshi** enterprises in the Tuticorin and Tirunelveli regions.

Therefore, the correct options are (i) and (iii), making option 1 the correct choice.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-324.q: Acharya Vinoba Bhave was one of the most prominent humanist and social reformers of modern India. He was born on __________
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-324.explanation:
**Acharya Vinoba Bhave**, a pioneer of the **Bhoodan Movement** and the first individual **Satyagrahi** chosen by Mahatma Gandhi, was born on **11 September 1895**.

He was born in the village of **Gagode** in the Raigad district of present-day **Maharashtra**. His birth name was **Vinayak Narahari Bhave**.

He is widely celebrated for his philosophy of **Sarvodaya**, which emphasizes the welfare of all people. His lifelong dedication to non-violence and social equality earned him the **Bharat Ratna** posthumously in 1983.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-325.q: The name ‘Pakistan’ or ‘Pak-stan’ was coined by a Punjabi student at Cambridge. Who was he?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-325.explanation:
The correct answer is **Choudhry Rahmat Ali**.

The term **Pakistan** was first introduced in the pamphlet titled **Now or Never; Are We to Live or Perish Forever?**, which was published on January 28, 1933.

**Choudhry Rahmat Ali**, a student at the University of Cambridge, coined the name to represent the Muslim-majority regions of British India. He created the acronym using the names of these provinces:

* **P**unjab
* **A**fghania (North-West Frontier Province)
* **K**ashmir
* **S**indh
* Baluchis**tan**

The term was intended to be an acronym for the states he envisioned as independent from India. While prominent political figures like **Mohammed Ali Jinnah** eventually led the movement for a separate state, the intellectual origin of the name lies solely with **Rahmat Ali**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-326.q: Who led the civil Disobedience movement after Mahatma Gandhi's arrest in 1930?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-326.explanation:
The correct answer is **Abbas Tyabji**.

After **Mahatma Gandhi** was arrested on May 4, 1930, for his defiance of the **Salt Laws** at **Dandi**, he had already nominated **Abbas Tyabji**, a retired judge and a prominent freedom fighter, to lead the **Dandi Salt March** to the **Dharasana Salt Works**.

**Abbas Tyabji** served as the immediate successor to Gandhi in the leadership of the **Civil Disobedience Movement** following the historic arrest.

Here is why the other options are contextually different:

* **Sarojini Naidu** took over the leadership of the **Dharasana Satyagraha** immediately after the arrest of **Abbas Tyabji** shortly after he himself began the march.
* **Jawaharlal Nehru** was a key leader of the movement but was already under arrest by mid-April 1930, weeks before Gandhi’s arrest at Dandi.
* **Subhash Chandra Bose** was deeply involved in the independence movement but was not the designated successor for the leadership of this specific phase of the **Salt Satyagraha**.

**Abbas Tyabji** is often fondly remembered as the **Grand Old Man of Gujarat**. His selection by Gandhi underscores the diverse and inclusive nature of the leadership during the **Salt Satyagraha**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-327.q: “In a sense Akbar might be considered to be the Father of Indian Nationalism. At that time there was little nationality in the country and religion was a dividing factor. Akbar placed the ideal of a Common Indian nationhood above the claims of separatist religion”. Who said the above statement?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-327.explanation:
The statement regarding **Akbar** as the **Father of Indian Nationalism** was made by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

This viewpoint is found in his famous literary work, **The Discovery of India**.

In this book, Nehru analyzes the history of India to understand the roots of its national identity. He highlights how **Akbar** sought to create a unified state by transcending religious divides and fostering a sense of common citizenship.

**Key reasons for this perspective:**

* **Religious Tolerance:** Akbar promoted **Sulh-i-kul** (universal peace), which aimed to harmonize different religious beliefs rather than favoring one.
* **National Integration:** By eliminating the **Jizya** tax and recruiting talent regardless of religion, he moved away from sectarian governance.
* **Secular Outlook:** Nehru identified Akbar's policies as an early attempt to integrate India into a single political and social entity, which aligns with modern ideals of **nationalism**.

Other leaders like **Mahatma Gandhi** or **Subash Chandra Bose** focused more on the anti-colonial struggle of the 20th century, whereas **Jawaharlal Nehru** frequently looked at historical figures to define the cultural and political lineage of Indian secularism.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-328.q: “If I found myself entirely absorbed in the service of the community, the reason behind it was my desire for self realisation. I have made the religion of service my own, as I felt that God could be realized only through service and service for me was the service of India. Because it came to me without my seeking, because I had an aptitude for it”.
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-328.explanation:
The correct answer is **Mahatma Gandhi**.

This famous quote reflects **Gandhi’s** deep-rooted philosophy of **Karma Yoga**, where he viewed social service not as a burden, but as a spiritual necessity. He believed that the path to **self-realization** and finding God lies in selfless service to humanity, particularly the downtrodden.

Here is why this aligns with his ideology:

* **Service to India:** For Gandhi, service to the country was synonymous with service to God. He famously stated that he could not find God apart from the rest of humanity, so he chose to serve through politics and social reform.
* **Aptitude for Service:** He often described his political life as an accidental evolution, claiming he was drawn into the service of the community because it felt like a natural calling rather than a calculated career move.
* **Self-Realization:** His autobiography, *The Story of My Experiments with Truth*, consistently emphasizes that his activities in the public sphere were driven by his internal pursuit of spiritual growth and the realization of Truth.

**Swami Vivekananda** also emphasized service, but his teachings primarily focused on **Vedanta** and the idea that service to man is service to God (*Daridra Narayana*). However, the specific framing of this quote regarding the "service of India" and the context of his political journey is characteristically **Gandhi**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-329.q: As a lawyer Mohandas Karam Chand Gandhi, got his-first fees of Rs. 30, but he refunded that to his client in __________ court
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-329.explanation:
The correct answer is **Bombay** (Mumbai).

After returning from England as a qualified barrister, **M.K. Gandhi** started his legal practice in **Bombay High Court**.

During his early days in Bombay, he suffered from stage fright and struggled to cross-examine witnesses. Because of this lack of confidence, he was unable to articulate his arguments effectively in the courtroom.

Feeling that he had failed his client due to his nervousness, he felt morally obligated to return the fees he had received. He handed the **Rs. 30** back to his client, marking a defining moment of integrity in his early professional career.

Following this experience, he moved to **Rajkot** to work as a legal drafter, which helped him build the confidence he eventually used in his later legal career in **South Africa**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-330.q:
Which of the following about Kamaraj are true?
i) He was arrested under Section 74 of Salt Act
ii) He was released on March 12, 1931
iii) He came to be closely associated with Rajaji during the election of 1926
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-330.explanation:
The correct answer is **(i) and (ii)**.

**K. Kamaraj**, the legendary leader of Tamil Nadu, was deeply involved in the freedom struggle. He was arrested under **Section 74 of the Salt Act** for his active participation in the **Salt Satyagraha** movement.

Following the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**, he was released from prison on **March 12, 1931**. These two events are well-documented milestones in his early political life.

Statement (iii) is incorrect because his close political association with **S. Satyamurti** was the defining factor during the 1926 elections, not **Rajaji**.

Related Facts:
* **Kamaraj** served as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu for three consecutive terms.
* He is widely remembered as the **Kingmaker** of Indian politics for his role in national leadership selection.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-331.q: At the London Museum, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s statue was attached with the statue of
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-331.explanation:
The correct answer is **Karl Marx**. In the **London Museum**, the statue of **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** stands alongside that of **Karl Marx**.

This placement holds great significance as both figures were revolutionary thinkers who dedicated their lives to addressing social inequality, justice, and the rights of the marginalized. Their proximity in the museum symbolizes the global recognition of their intellectual contributions to social and political thought.

The other options, **Vincent Churchill**, **Abraham Lincoln**, and **Lord Bentinck**, are historical figures, but they are not the individuals paired with Ambedkar in this specific memorial display.

Related Facts:
* **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** is the chief architect of the **Indian Constitution**.
* **Karl Marx** is best known for his influential work, **Das Kapital**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-332.q: British arrested Subash Chandra Bose on 24% October 1924 A.D. and sent him to __________ Jail
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-332.explanation:
The correct answer is **Mandalay**.

In October 1924, the British government arrested **Subhash Chandra Bose** under the **Bengal Criminal Law Amendment Act**. They suspected his involvement in revolutionary activities and sought to curb the growing nationalist movement in Bengal.

Following his arrest, he was deported to **Mandalay Jail** in present-day **Myanmar** (then part of British India). He remained imprisoned there for nearly three years, during which time his health significantly deteriorated.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Tihar Jail** is located in Delhi and was established much later, in 1957.
* **Andaman** (specifically the **Cellular Jail**) is famous for housing revolutionaries, but Bose was not sent there in 1924.
* **Kolkata** (then Calcutta) was where he was arrested, not where he was incarcerated during this specific period of exile.

This period in **Mandalay Jail** was a formative time for Bose, often compared to the imprisonment of **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** at the same facility years earlier. It deepened his resolve and solidified his stature as a major leader in the Indian freedom struggle.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-333.q: The Marathi fortnightly newspaper ‘Bahishkrit Bharat’ was started by
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-333.explanation:
The correct answer is **B.R. Ambedkar**.

He launched the Marathi fortnightly newspaper **Bahishkrit Bharat** (meaning "Ostracized India") in **1927**. This publication was a crucial platform for his movement to uplift the **Dalit** community and advocate for their social and political rights.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Mahatma Gandhi**: While he was a prolific journalist who edited newspapers like *Young India* and *Harijan*, he was not associated with the founding of *Bahishkrit Bharat*.
* **Jyotirao Phule**: A pioneer of social reform, he died in 1890, decades before this newspaper was established.
* **Kaivartas**: This refers to a community rather than an individual political leader or journalist.

**Ambedkar** used his journalism to challenge the **caste system** and demand equality. Other notable periodicals started by him include **Mooknayak** (1920) and **Janata** (1930).

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-334.q: Gandhiji established an ashram at Sabarmathi. Likewise an ashram was established in Tamil Nadu by Rajaji. Where was it established?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-334.explanation:
The correct location is **Tiruchengode**.

**C. Rajagopalachari**, popularly known as **Rajaji**, founded the **Gandhi Ashram** at **Tiruchengode** in the present-day **Namakkal district** in **1925**.

He established this center to promote the ideals of the **Non-Cooperation Movement**, encourage **Khadi** production, and foster social reforms like the removal of untouchability.

Here is why the other options do not fit:

* **Madurai:** While a significant center for the freedom struggle, it is not the site of Rajaji's specific ashram.
* **Vedaranyam:** This location is famous for the **Salt Satyagraha** march led by Rajaji in **1930**, but it was not the site of his permanent ashram.
* **Salem:** This was Rajaji's hometown and base of political activity, but the specific ashram institution was established in the nearby town of **Tiruchengode**.

The **Tiruchengode Gandhi Ashram** remains an important historical site today, reflecting the spread of Gandhian constructive programs in Tamil Nadu.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-335.q:
Which of the following are correctly paired?
i) New India and Commonweal - Mrs. Annie Besant
ii) Kesari and Maratha - Bala Gangadhar Tilak
iii) Indian Opinion - Gopal Hari Deshmukh
iv) Indu Prakash - Mahatma Gandhi
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-335.explanation:
The correct pairs are **(i)** and **(ii)**, which makes the first option the right choice.

**Mrs. Annie Besant** was a prominent leader of the Home Rule Movement and established the newspapers **New India** and **Commonweal** to propagate her political ideas and nationalist sentiment.

**Bal Gangadhar Tilak** founded the newspapers **Kesari** (published in Marathi) and **Maratha** (published in English) to mobilize public opinion against British colonial rule and awaken national consciousness.

Regarding the incorrect pairs:
* **Indian Opinion** was established by **Mahatma Gandhi** during his time in South Africa, not Gopal Hari Deshmukh.
* **Indu Prakash** was a prominent newspaper associated with **Mahadev Govind Ranade** and **Vishnu Parashuram Shastri Pandit**, not Mahatma Gandhi.

These newspapers played a crucial role in the **Indian Freedom Struggle** by serving as powerful tools for communication, political education, and social reform across the country.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-336.q: “British rule was established in India with the cooperation of Indians, and had survived only because of this co-operation. If Indians refused to co-operate, British rule in India would collapse within a year and Swaraj would come,” who said this?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-336.explanation:
The correct answer is **Mahatma Gandhiji**. This statement is a cornerstone of the philosophy behind the **Non-Cooperation Movement** launched in 1920.

In his seminal work **Hind Swaraj**, published in 1909, **Mahatma Gandhi** articulated his core belief that the British administration in India was entirely dependent on the willing participation and support of the Indian people.

Here is why this is the correct perspective:

* **Strategic Passive Resistance**: Gandhi argued that by withdrawing support from government schools, law courts, and administrative bodies, Indians could effectively render the colonial machinery powerless.
* **The Concept of Swaraj**: He believed that true self-rule (**Swaraj**) would be achieved not through violent revolution, but by a moral and political withdrawal of cooperation from an unjust system.
* **Non-Violent Non-Cooperation**: This specific quote served as the moral foundation for the **Non-Cooperation Movement**, which sought to challenge British authority through peaceful civil disobedience.

The other options are incorrect because:

* **Motilal Nehru** was a key leader in the Swaraj Party, but he focused more on parliamentary obstructionism from within the legislatures rather than this specific ideological call for total non-cooperation.
* **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** and **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** played immense roles in the freedom struggle, but this specific quote is synonymous with the core political philosophy of **Mahatma Gandhi**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-337.q: What is the title of the Doctoral Thesis of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1923?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-337.explanation:
The correct title of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's doctoral thesis, submitted to the **London School of Economics** in 1923, is **The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution**.

Here is why this is the correct choice:

*   **Academic Achievement**: Dr. Ambedkar earned his **Doctor of Science (D.Sc.)** degree for this rigorous economic study. It remains a seminal work on the history of Indian currency and monetary policy.
*   **Historical Context**: The thesis analyzes the evolution of the Indian currency system, specifically the transition from the silver standard to the gold exchange standard, and critiques the colonial economic policies of the time.

Regarding the other options:

*   **Caste system and Untouchability**: While these were central themes in his sociological and political writings (such as *Annihilation of Caste*), they were not the subject of his 1923 doctoral thesis.
*   **Unbritish Rule in India**: This is the famous work written by **Dadabhai Naoroji**, which popularized the **Drain Theory**, explaining how British colonial rule led to the economic impoverishment of India.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-338.q: Name the biographical work of Abdul Kalam Azad which was written during his internment in 1916
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-338.explanation:
The biographical work written by **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** during his internment in Ranchi between 1916 and 1920 is titled **Tazkira**.

This work is highly significant as it provides deep insights into the history of his family and his early life. **Tazkira** was penned during a period of enforced isolation when the British colonial government restricted his movements due to his anti-colonial activities.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

*   **Kadith** is not a biographical work associated with Azad.
*   **Hayy Ibn Yaqdhan** is a famous philosophical novel written by the philosopher **Ibn Tufail** in the 12th century.
*   **Kitab al-Miraj** is an Islamic text concerning the Prophet Muhammad's night journey and ascension to heaven, not a biography by Azad.

**Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** was a towering intellectual and a key leader in the **Indian National Movement**. He later served as the first **Minister of Education** in independent India. His literary contributions, including his famous newspaper **Al-Hilal** and his autobiography **India Wins Freedom**, remain essential reading for understanding Indian history and political thought.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-339.q:
Which of the following statements are true about Mahatma Gandhi?
i) He faced racial discrimination for the 1st time in Pietermaritzburg railway station.
ii) He launched a struggle against unjust laws in Transvaal.
iii) He deeply influenced by Ruskin, and established the Phoenix settlement in 1905.
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-339.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4: **(i), (ii), and (iii) are correct**.

*   **Pietermaritzburg Incident**: In 1893, Mahatma Gandhi was famously thrown off a train at **Pietermaritzburg station** in South Africa because he refused to leave the first-class compartment. This event was a turning point that sparked his commitment to fighting racial discrimination.

*   **Transvaal Struggle**: Gandhi organized the Indian community in **Transvaal** to resist the **Asiatic Registration Act** of 1906, which required Indians to register and carry certificates. This marked the formal beginning of his **Satyagraha** movement.

*   **Phoenix Settlement and Ruskin**: Gandhi was profoundly influenced by John Ruskin’s book *Unto This Last*. Inspired by these ideas, he founded the **Phoenix Settlement** near Durban in 1904 (often cited as 1905 in historical literature regarding its full operation) to promote communal living and equality.

Since all three statements accurately reflect key milestones in Gandhi's life in South Africa, they are all correct.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-340.q: The author of the book ‘Why I am an Atheist’?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-340.explanation:
The correct author of the book **Why I am an Atheist** is **Bhagat Singh**.

This essay was written by the Indian revolutionary **Bhagat Singh** while he was imprisoned in **Lahore Jail** in 1930. He penned this work in response to accusations from fellow prisoners and religious figures that his lack of belief in God was a result of his vanity or pride.

In the essay, **Bhagat Singh** provides a rational and logical defense of **atheism**. He argues that belief in a deity is a product of human ignorance and a tool used to maintain social order and justify oppressive structures. He asserts that true freedom requires an individual to question traditional dogmas and rely on human reasoning.

Regarding the other options:

* **E.V.R. Periyar** was a prominent social reformer and a staunch rationalist who advocated for self-respect and atheism in Tamil Nadu, but he is not the author of this specific text.
* **C.N. Annadurai** was a key political figure and founder of the DMK, known for his oratory skills and secular ideals, but he did not write this book.
* **Rajaguru** was a close revolutionary associate of **Bhagat Singh** who participated in the struggle against British rule, but he is not associated with this literary work.

This piece remains a seminal text in Indian political thought, emphasizing the importance of **scientific temper** and **critical thinking** over blind faith.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-341.q:
Which of the following statements are true about V.O. Chidambaram Pillai?
i) He was a follower of Gopalakrishna Gokhale.
ii) He was known as Chekkiluththa Chemmal.
iii) He founded the servants of India Society.
iv) He was a lawyer.
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-341.explanation:
The correct answer is **(ii)** and **(iv)** only.

**V.O. Chidambaram Pillai**, popularly known as **Kappalottiya Thamizhan**, was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and a **lawyer** by profession, based in Thoothukudi.

Regarding the specific statements:

*   **He was known as Chekkiluththa Chemmal:** This statement is **true**. This title translates to "the person who pulled the oil press," referring to his brutal imprisonment by the British where he was forced to perform manual labor.
*   **He was a lawyer:** This statement is **true**. He was an active legal practitioner before dedicating his life fully to the Indian National Movement.

Regarding the incorrect statements:

*   **He was a follower of Gopalakrishna Gokhale:** This is **false**. V.O. Chidambaram Pillai was a staunch follower of **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** and belonged to the extremist wing of the Indian National Congress.
*   **He founded the Servants of India Society:** This is **false**. The **Servants of India Society** was founded by **Gopalakrishna Gokhale** in 1905 to promote social and human development.

Since statements (ii) and (iv) are correct, and they appear as option 3 in the provided list, this identifies the accurate facts about his life and political affiliations.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-342.q: Who founded the Indian National Army?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-342.explanation:
The **Indian National Army (INA)**, also known as the **Azad Hind Fauj**, was originally founded by **Captain Mohan Singh** in 1942.

He established the force in Southeast Asia after the fall of Singapore, drawing primarily from captured Indian prisoners of war who were fighting for the British.

Although **Subash Chandra Bose** is the figure most famously associated with the INA, he did not establish it. He took over the leadership of the INA from Rash Behari Bose in 1943 and revitalized the movement, but the foundation occurred under Mohan Singh's initiative.

**Shah Nawaz Khan** and **P.K. Sehgal** were prominent officers within the INA who served as key commanders under Subash Chandra Bose, but they were not the original founders.

In summary, **Col. Mohan Singh** is recognized as the visionary who initiated the formation of the army to fight for India's independence from British rule.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-343.q: __________ Newspaper was started by Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-343.explanation:
The correct answer is **National Herald**.

**Jawaharlal Nehru** established the **National Herald** in **1938** in Lucknow. The primary purpose of this newspaper was to advocate for the **Indian independence movement** and to support the policies of the **Indian National Congress**.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

*   **Commonweal** was a weekly newspaper started by **Annie Besant** in 1914 to promote the Home Rule movement.
*   **Young India** was a weekly journal published by **Mahatma Gandhi** from 1919 to 1931.
*   **Khadar** refers to hand-spun and hand-woven cloth (**Khadi**), which became a symbol of self-reliance and the Swadeshi movement, not a newspaper.

The **National Herald** played a significant role in shaping public opinion during the colonial era and remained an important voice for the Congress party for many decades.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-344.q: Allan Octavian Hume presided over the meeting of the theosophical society in Madras in the year
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-344.explanation:
**Allan Octavian Hume** was deeply associated with the **Theosophical Society** during his time in India. Following the annual convention of the society held at Adyar, Madras, in **December 1884**, Hume presided over a significant post-convention meeting.

This event is historically notable because it occurred just before the formation of the **Indian National Congress**. At this gathering, prominent leaders discussed the idea of creating a national platform for political deliberation.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **October 1885**: By this time, the focus had shifted toward the direct preparations for the first session of the Indian National Congress, which took place in December 1885.
* **November 1887 and March 1888**: These dates do not align with the specific historical record of Hume’s leadership at the Theosophical Society headquarters in Madras.

The 1884 convention was a landmark moment as it brought together intellectuals and reformers, providing the intellectual climate and social networks that eventually led to the birth of the **INC** in 1885.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-345.q: What is the name of Bhagatsingh’s Mother?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-345.explanation:
The mother of the revolutionary freedom fighter **Bhagat Singh** was **Vidyavati**. She is often referred to as "Punjab Mata" for her immense sacrifices and for raising a son who became a national icon.

Here is a quick look at why the other names do not fit this context:

* **Lilavati**: This name is associated with various historical figures but is not linked to Bhagat Singh’s immediate family.
* **Bhuvaneswari**: This was the mother of **Subhas Chandra Bose**, a prominent leader in the Indian National Movement.
* **Lakshmi Kaur**: This name does not correspond to the mother of Bhagat Singh.

**Vidyavati** played a significant role in nurturing the spirit of patriotism in her children. Her resilience during Bhagat Singh's imprisonment and his subsequent execution at the age of 23 left a lasting impact on the Indian independence movement.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-346.q: Which National Leader of India who died on 27 May 1964?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-346.explanation:
The correct answer is **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

**Jawaharlal Nehru**, the first Prime Minister of independent India, passed away on **27 May 1964**. He served as the Prime Minister from the time of independence in 1947 until his death.

Here is why the other options are incorrect based on their death dates:

* **B.R. Ambedkar**: The primary architect of the Indian Constitution passed away on **6 December 1956**.
* **E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar)**: The father of the Self-Respect Movement passed away on **24 December 1973**.
* **Abul Kalam Azad**: The first Minister of Education in the Indian government passed away on **22 February 1958**.

**Jawaharlal Nehru** is widely remembered for his role in shaping modern India, his policy of **Non-Alignment**, and his vision for **industrialization** through Five-Year Plans. His birthday, **14 November**, is celebrated across India as **Children's Day**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-347.q: __________ spread Theosophical ideas through her newspapers called "New India" and "Common weal"
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-347.explanation:
The correct answer is **Annie Besant**.

**Annie Besant** was a prominent British socialist, theosophist, and women's rights activist who played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement. She joined the **Theosophical Society** in 1889 and later became its President.

To promote her vision and spread Theosophical ideas, she founded two influential newspapers:

*   **New India**: A daily newspaper used to advocate for **Home Rule** and social reforms.
*   **Commonweal**: A weekly journal focused on political and social issues in India.

Regarding the other options:

*   **Savitri Bai Phule** was a pioneer in women's education and social reform in Maharashtra, particularly known for her work with her husband, **Jyotirao Phule**.
*   **Ayyan Kali** was a prominent social reformer from Kerala who fought against the caste system and worked for the upliftment of the **Dalit** community.
*   **Sir Sayyid Ahmed Khan** was a key figure in the **Aligarh Movement**, focused on modernizing education for Indian Muslims and promoting scientific temper.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-348.explanation:
The correct answer is **Subramaniya Bharathiyar - December 11, 1881**.

This pair is incorrect because **Subramaniya Bharathiyar** was born on **December 11, 1882**, not 1881. Knowing the birth years of our freedom fighters is essential for historical chronology in your TNPSC preparation.

The other options provide accurate historical data regarding the birth dates of these prominent figures:
* **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai** was born on September 5, 1872.
* **C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji)** was born on December 10, 1878.
* **K. Kamarajar** was born on July 15, 1903.

Related Facts:
* **V.O. Chidambaram** is famously known as the *Kappalottiya Thamizhan*.
* **K. Kamarajar** is celebrated as the *Kingmaker* of Indian politics.
* **Subramaniya Bharathiyar** is widely revered as the *Mahakavi* (Great Poet) of Tamil literature.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-349.q: Which one of the following is the family name of Nehru?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-349.explanation:
The correct answer is **Kaul**.

The **Nehru** family originally belonged to the **Kaul** lineage of Kashmiri Brahmins. In the early 18th century, **Raj Kaul**, an ancestor of Jawaharlal Nehru, migrated from Kashmir to Delhi.

He settled near a canal (*nehar*) in the city, which led to the family adopting the surname **Nehru**—a derivation of the word *nehar*.

*   **Rai** is a common title or surname in North India, often denoting nobility or royalty, but it is not the ancestral name of the Nehru family.
*   **Kul** means "family" or "clan" in Sanskrit, but it is not a specific surname associated with the Nehru lineage.
*   **Sarkar** is a title meaning government or master, frequently used in various regions of India as a respectful address, but it is unrelated to the Nehru family's history.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-350.q:
Choose the correct statements :
1) Bharathi edited a Tamil weekly ‘India’. Which became the voice of the moderates
2) Bharathi participated the Surat session of congress in 1907
3) Chakravartini, Swadesamitran Newspapers was edited by Bharathi
4) G.Subramaniya Iyer Published newspaper The Hindu
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-350.explanation:
The correct answer is **2, 3, and 4 only**.

* **Bharathi** attended the **1907 Surat session** of the Indian National Congress, which is a historically significant event where the party split between Moderates and Extremists.
* **Bharathi** worked as an editor for journals like ***Chakravartini*** and ***Swadesamitran***, playing a vital role in Tamil journalism.
* **G. Subramaniya Iyer** founded and published the newspaper ***The Hindu*** in 1878 to mobilize public opinion against British policies.

The first statement is incorrect because the weekly magazine ***India***, edited by Bharathi, was the voice of the **Extremists** (Garams), not the Moderates.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-351.q:
Assertion (A) : Ramachandra Guha calls Kumarappa as “Green Gandhian”.
Reason (R) : Kumarappa was the founder of modern environmentalism in India.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-351.explanation:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

**Ramachandra Guha**, a renowned historian, explicitly referred to **J.C. Kumarappa** as the '**Green Gandhian**'. This title highlights Kumarappa's dedication to sustainable development and his critique of industrialization, which laid the ideological foundation for environmental awareness in India.

**Kumarappa** advocated for a decentralized economic model that prioritized rural self-sufficiency and ecological balance. His work serves as the primary inspiration for modern Indian environmentalism, making the reason a valid and accurate explanation for the assertion.

Other options are incorrect because both the statement regarding his title and his pioneering role in environmental thought are historically accurate and causally linked.

**Related Facts:**
* Kumarappa wrote the influential book **Economy of Permanence**.
* He was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and a key figure in the **All India Village Industries Association**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-352.q: Which of the following statements, Lokmanya Tilak, wrote in his papers Kesari and Mahratta, are true?
options: The victory of the coral mill workers
The victory of the Dandi salt sathyagraha
The victory of the vedaranyam salt sathyagraha
The success of the Swadeshi Navigation company
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-352.explanation:
The correct answer is **The victory of the coral mill workers**. Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak used his newspapers, **Kesari** and **Mahratta**, to champion the cause of laborers and promote the **Swadeshi movement**.

He specifically highlighted the **Coral Mill strike** in Tuticorin, which occurred around 1908. Through his writings, he supported the workers' struggle against oppressive colonial labor conditions and encouraged the spirit of nationalism.

Other options are incorrect because:
* The **Dandi salt satyagraha** (1930) and **Vedaranyam salt satyagraha** (1930) took place well after Tilak's death in 1920.
* While he supported the **Swadeshi movement**, the specific victory of the **Swadeshi Navigation company** is distinct from the coverage he provided to the Coral Mill labor agitation.

Related Facts:
* **Kesari** was published in Marathi, while **Mahratta** was published in English.
* Tilak was famously known for the slogan, "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it."

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-353.q:
Assertion [A] : Besides being a political Leader, Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a great Social Reformer.
Reason [R] : He was one of the founders of the distinguished organisation known as “The Servants of India Society”.
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-353.explanation:
The correct answer is that **both [A] and [R] are true**, making the third option the correct choice.

**Gopal Krishna Gokhale** was indeed a prominent **political leader**, serving as a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi and leading the moderate faction of the Indian National Congress.

Beyond politics, he was a dedicated **social reformer** who believed that political progress was inseparable from social advancement. He campaigned tirelessly for education, the abolition of the caste system, and the upliftment of the marginalized sections of society.

He founded the **Servants of India Society** in **1905** in Pune. The primary objective of this organization was to train national missionaries for the service of India and to promote social and human development through selfless, constitutional means.

Since the **Servants of India Society** was established specifically to carry out his social reform agenda, the reason provided directly supports the assertion that he was a great social reformer.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-354.q:
Which of the following statements are true about Madasamy?
i) He was the right hand of V.0.C
ii) He escaped to Germany
iii) He participated in the Non Cooperation Movement.
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-354.explanation:
**Madasamy**, a brave freedom fighter from Tamil Nadu, is historically recognized for his close association with the nationalist leader **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai (V.O.C.)**. He served as a trusted associate during the intense period of the **Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company** struggle.

Regarding the given statements:

*   **Statement (i) is true**: Madasamy was indeed a key aide and the right hand of **V.O.C.** during the anti-British movements in Tuticorin.
*   **Statement (ii) is true**: In a bid to evade colonial arrest and gather international support for the Indian independence movement, he managed to escape to **Germany**.
*   **Statement (iii) is false**: Madasamy's primary revolutionary activities took place much earlier during the **Swadeshi movement** (1906–1911), rather than the **Non-Cooperation Movement** which gained momentum under Gandhi in 1920.

Since both statements (i) and (ii) are accurate, the correct option is **1**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-355.q:
Which of the following is incorrectly paired?
1) Vivekananda - Ramakrishna mission
2) Swami Dayanand Saraswati - Theosophical society
3) H.P. Blavatsky - Aryasamaj
4) Sayyid Ahmad Khan - Muhammadan Anglo Oriental college
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-355.explanation:
The correct answer is **(2) and (3)**. These options are incorrectly paired because the founders have been switched.

* **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** founded the **Arya Samaj** in 1875, not the Theosophical Society.
* **H.P. Blavatsky** was one of the co-founders of the **Theosophical Society** in 1875, not the Arya Samaj.

Options (1) and (4) are correct pairs. Swami Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 to propagate the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa. Similarly, Sir Sayyid Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in Aligarh in 1875, which later grew into the Aligarh Muslim University.

Related Facts:
* The Arya Samaj focused on the authority of the Vedas and monotheism.
* The Theosophical Society promoted the study of comparative religion and philosophy.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-356.q:
Arrange the following events related to K. Kamaraj in their chronological order
1) K. Kamaraj was chosen to lead the struggle against the Neill statue after the arrest of other frontline leaders.
2) He was arrested for enlisting volunteers for salt satyagraha.
3) He was arrested at Guntur while he was on his way to Wardha.
4) He was accused in an inter provincial conspiracy case known as ‘Madras conspiracy case’.
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-356.explanation:
To understand the chronological progression of K. Kamaraj's political journey during the freedom struggle, let us analyze the events in sequence:

*   **The Neill Statue Satyagraha (1927):** This was one of Kamaraj's early involvements in the freedom movement. After senior leaders were arrested, he took charge of the agitation to remove the statue of Colonel Neill in Madras. This represents the earliest event in the list.

*   **Salt Satyagraha (1930):** Following the Dandi March initiated by Gandhi, Kamaraj actively enlisted volunteers for the salt satyagraha in Tamil Nadu. His role in organizing these efforts led to his arrest and imprisonment in Alipore jail.

*   **The Madras Conspiracy Case (1933):** Kamaraj was accused in this case, which investigated revolutionary activities against British rule. Being linked to this conspiracy reflects his intensified participation in the independence movement during the early 1930s.

*   **Arrest at Guntur (1940):** During the individual satyagraha movement, Kamaraj was on his way to meet Mahatma Gandhi at Wardha to seek instructions. He was intercepted and arrested at Guntur railway station, marking a later stage of his political activism.

Based on this timeline:
1. Neill Statue (1927)
2. Salt Satyagraha (1930)
4. Madras Conspiracy Case (1933)
3. Arrest at Guntur (1940)

Therefore, the correct sequence of events is 1, 2, 4, 3.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-357.q:
Match :
A) Mahadev Govind Ranade - 1) The mystic dreamer of dreams
B) Gopala Krishna Gokhale - 2) Socrates of Maharashtra
C) Bala Gangadhar Tilak - 3) The Lion of the Punjab
D) Lala Lajpat Rai - 4) Uncrowned king of India
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-357.explanation:
The correct matching for these historical figures is as follows:

*   **Mahadev Govind Ranade** is known as the **Socrates of Maharashtra**. His intellectual depth and role as a mentor to many nationalists earned him this title (A-2).

*   **Gopala Krishna Gokhale** was often described as **the mystic dreamer of dreams**. This phrase reflects his visionary approach to politics and his role as the political guru to Mahatma Gandhi (B-1).

*   **Bala Gangadhar Tilak** was famously known as the **Uncrowned king of India** (or *Lokamanya*). His radical leadership and immense popularity among the masses led to this title (C-4).

*   **Lala Lajpat Rai** is historically celebrated as **The Lion of the Punjab** (*Punjab Kesari*). He was a key leader in the extremist wing of the Congress and a fierce advocate for independence (D-3).

Matching these points, we get A-2, B-1, C-4, and D-3. This corresponds to the third option provided in your list.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-358.q:
Consider the following Statements, Choose the correct answer :
i) January 30 is the Death anniversary of Annal Gandhi Adigal.
ii) January 23rd is the Birth Anniversary of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose.
iii) April 14th is the Birth Anniversary of Annal Ambedkar.
iv) October 13th is the Birth Anniversary of Sardar Vallabhai Patel.
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-358.explanation:
The correct answer is **(i), (ii), and (iii) only are correct**.

Here is the breakdown of the statements:

*   **January 30** is observed as **Martyrs' Day** (Shaheed Diwas) in India, marking the death anniversary of **Mahatma Gandhi**, who is referred to as **Annal Gandhi Adigal** in Tamil. This statement is **correct**.

*   **January 23** marks the birth anniversary of **Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose**. The Government of India celebrates this day as **Parakram Diwas**. This statement is **correct**.

*   **April 14** is the birth anniversary of **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, the principal architect of the Indian Constitution. It is celebrated as **Ambedkar Jayanti** across the country. This statement is **correct**.

*   **October 31** is the birth anniversary of **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, celebrated as **National Unity Day** (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas). The statement mentions October 13, which makes it **incorrect**.

Since statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are factual, the correct choice is the option that includes these three.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-359.q: Identify the person who uttered that, “Nothing can be done without shedding of blood. Japan was prepared to sacrifice 20,000 men and gained a victory over Russia. If 15 crores of Indians do the same, “Swaraj will be obtained”.
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-359.explanation:
The correct answer is **Subramania Siva**.

**Subramania Siva** was a fearless freedom fighter and a close associate of V.O. Chidambaram Pillai. He played a vital role in the Swadeshi movement in Tamil Nadu and often used powerful rhetoric to inspire the masses towards the goal of **Swaraj** (self-rule).

He famously invoked the example of Japan's victory over Russia in the Russo-Japanese War to demonstrate the power of sacrifice. He believed that if a massive population like India's committed to the cause with the same level of dedication as the Japanese soldiers, freedom would be inevitable.

* **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai** is known for starting the first indigenous Indian shipping service.
* **Subramania Bharathi** is celebrated for his revolutionary poetry and nationalist writings.
* **Vanchi Aiyar** is known for his role in the assassination of Robert Ashe.

Related Facts:
* Subramania Siva was a staunch advocate of the **Swadeshi movement**.
* He spent several years in prison for his revolutionary activities against British colonial rule.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-360.q:
Choose the right matches :
1) Ferosha Metha - Disciple of Gokhale
2) Gopala Krishna Gokhale - Servants of India Society
3) Dadabhai Naoroji - Drain Theory
4) S.N. Banerjee - Safety Valve Theory
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-360.explanation:
The correct answer is **(2) and (3) are correct**. Here is the breakdown of the pairs provided:

*   **Gopala Krishna Gokhale - Servants of India Society**: This is **correct**. Gokhale founded the **Servants of India Society** in 1905 to promote social and human development and prepare national missionaries for the service of India.

*   **Dadabhai Naoroji - Drain Theory**: This is **correct**. Naoroji, often called the **Grand Old Man of India**, articulated the **Drain Theory** in his work *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*, explaining how wealth was being siphoned from India to Britain.

*   **Ferosha Metha - Disciple of Gokhale**: This is **incorrect**. While Ferozeshah Mehta and Gokhale were both prominent **Moderates** in the Indian National Congress, Mehta was not a disciple of Gokhale. Gokhale himself was the disciple of **M.G. Ranade**.

*   **S.N. Banerjee - Safety Valve Theory**: This is **incorrect**. The **Safety Valve Theory** is associated with A.O. Hume. It suggests that the British government allowed the formation of the Indian National Congress as a mechanism to vent public discontent and prevent a violent uprising like that of 1857. S.N. Banerjee was a founding member and a prominent leader of the Congress, but he did not originate this theory.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-361.q:
False statements about Subhas Chandra Bose are:
i) Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23 January 1897, in Calcutta, West Bengal.
ii) The Government of India has declared his birthday, 23rd January as “Parakram Diwas”.
iii) To honour Subhas Chandra Bose’s legacy, 23 January is a National holiday.
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-361.explanation:
The correct answer is **(i) and (iii) only**.

* **Subhas Chandra Bose** was born on **23 January 1897** in **Cuttack**, Odisha, not in Calcutta (now Kolkata), West Bengal. This makes statement (i) false.
* The Government of India celebrates his birthday, **23 January**, as **Parakram Diwas** (Day of Valour) to honor his courage. Statement (ii) is correct.
* While 23 January is celebrated as **Parakram Diwas**, it is not officially declared a **National Holiday** throughout India. Therefore, statement (iii) is false.

Related Facts:
* **Subhas Chandra Bose** was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement and the founder of the **Azad Hind Fauj** (Indian National Army).
* He famously gave the slogan **Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!**.

questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-362.q: Who organized “Khudai Khidmatgar” in North West Frontier Provinces?
questions/inm-emergence-of-leaders-362.explanation:
The correct answer is **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**.

He established the **Khudai Khidmatgar** movement, which translates to "Servants of God," in the **North West Frontier Province (NWFP)** during the 1930s.

Here are the key points to remember about this movement:

*   It was a **non-violent** movement aimed at social reform and gaining independence from British rule.
*   The members were also known as **Red Shirts** because of the color of their uniforms.
*   **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** is popularly known as **Frontier Gandhi** or *Badshah Khan* due to his adherence to Gandhian principles of non-violence and his leadership in the region.

**Why the others are incorrect:**
