questions/tn-econ-trend-135-031.q: In which year the Self respect movement was rechristened as Dravidar Kazhagam?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-031.explanation:
The correct year for this transition is **1944**.

During the **Salem Conference** held in August **1944**, **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy** proposed a resolution to rename the **Justice Party** and the **Self-Respect Movement** as **Dravidar Kazhagam** (DK).

This change was formalised under the leadership of **Periyar** and **C.N. Annadurai**, marking a significant shift in the political landscape of Tamil Nadu.

The primary objective behind this change was to establish a dedicated social movement focused on **Dravidian identity**, rationalism, and social justice.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:
* **1933** was a period when the Self-Respect Movement was actively building its base but had not yet adopted the identity of Dravidar Kazhagam.
* **1955** and **1966** occurred long after the formation of the **Dravidar Kazhagam**, by which time the party had already been established as a prominent socio-political force.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-032.q: Who was one of the prominent leaders from the depressed class?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-032.explanation:
The correct leader from the provided options associated with the upliftment of the depressed classes is **M.C. Raja**.

**M.C. Raja** (Mylai Chinna Thambi Raja) was a pioneering leader of the **Depressed Classes movement** in the Madras Presidency. He played a crucial role in advocating for the rights of the marginalized communities, specifically the Adi Dravidas.

Here is why the other figures differ:

* **Subramanya Bharathi** was a legendary poet and freedom fighter known for his nationalist writings and social reformism, particularly regarding women's rights and caste-based discrimination, but he is not primarily classified as a leader of the depressed class movement itself.
* **Thanthai Periyar** led the **Self-Respect Movement**, which fought against caste-based discrimination and Brahminical dominance, but he is fundamentally recognized for the broader Self-Respect and Dravidian ideologies.
* **M.G. Ranade** was a prominent social reformer and one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress, active primarily in the Indian Social Conference in Maharashtra.

**M.C. Raja** was instrumental in the legislative efforts to secure representation and education for depressed classes, famously becoming the first elected representative of the depressed classes in the Madras Legislative Council. He is often remembered alongside **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** for his nationwide contributions to Dalit empowerment during the pre-independence era.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-033.q: Which party was merged with the self respect movement?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-033.explanation:
The correct answer is **Justice Party**. In 1944, at the Salem conference, **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy** proposed changing the name of the **Justice Party** to **Dravida Kazhagam**. This marked the merger of the **Self-Respect Movement** with the **Justice Party** to foster social equality and anti-caste sentiments.

* **Dravida Pandiyan** was not the primary party that merged with the movement.
* **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam** was actually formed later in 1949 as a breakaway group from the **Dravida Kazhagam**.
* **Dravida Kazhagam** is the new name the **Justice Party** adopted after the merger, not the party that merged with the movement.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-034.q: Rettaimalai Srinivasan was born in which year?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-034.explanation:
**Rettaimalai Srinivasan**, a prominent leader of the **Adi Dravida** movement, was born on July 7, **1859**. He was born in the village of **Chandrapuram** in the Madurai district of Tamil Nadu.

He is widely celebrated for his significant contributions to the social upliftment of the **depressed classes** and for his role as a pioneering social reformer. His life and work were dedicated to securing rights and dignity for the marginalized sections of society.

In 1893, he founded the **Adi Dravida Mahajana Sabha** to advocate for the rights of the oppressed. He also represented the **depressed classes** at the **Round Table Conferences** held in London alongside **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**.

He is also remembered as the author of his autobiography titled **Jeeviya Saritha Surukkam**, which is considered the first autobiography written by a Dalit person in Tamil.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-035.q: In which year the East India company gets the lease of Madras from a local king?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-035.explanation:
The correct year for the lease of Madras by the **East India Company** is **1639**.

*   **Francis Day**, an agent of the East India Company, obtained the grant of land known as **Madraspatnam** from the **Raja of Chandragiri**, who was the local ruler of that region.
*   The transaction allowed the British to build a fortified factory, which later became **Fort St. George**.
*   This establishment served as the primary administrative center for the British on the **Coromandel Coast**.

Option 1 (1629) is incorrect as it precedes the establishment of the settlement. Option 3 (1632) refers to the grant of the **Golden Farman** by the Sultan of Golconda, which allowed the British to trade in the region, but not the specific lease of Madras. Option 4 (1648) falls several years after the initial foundation of the site.

The year **1639** marks a pivotal moment in colonial history, as it effectively laid the foundation for British power in Southern India.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-036.q:
Choose the correct statement
Statement 1 : Ryotwari system was introduced by Thomas Munro
Statement 2 : In the Ryotwari system, the rights of ownership were handed over to the peasants
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-036.explanation:
The correct answer is **Both I and II**.

**Thomas Munro**, the Governor of Madras, introduced the **Ryotwari system** in 1820. This system was designed to establish a direct relationship between the government and the cultivators.

Under the **Ryotwari system**, the following principles applied:

*   **Direct Settlement**: The government dealt directly with the **Ryot** (cultivator) for the collection of land revenue.
*   **Ownership Rights**: The peasants were recognized as the actual **owners of the land**. As long as they paid the revenue, they held the right to sell, gift, or mortgage their land.
*   **Revenue Assessment**: The revenue was fixed for a period, typically 20 to 30 years, after which it was subject to revision based on soil quality and crop conditions.

Since the system granted proprietary rights to the peasants and was indeed pioneered by **Thomas Munro** in the Madras Presidency, both statements are factually accurate.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-037.q: In which year the Ilbert Bill was passed?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-037.explanation:
The correct answer is **1884**.

The **Ilbert Bill** was introduced in **1883** by **Lord Ripon** to allow Indian judges to try cases involving Europeans. Due to intense opposition from the European community in India, the bill faced significant modifications before it was finally passed in its diluted form in **1884**.

The other options are incorrect because **1883** marks the year it was first introduced, while **1885** and **1886** do not align with the historical enactment of this specific legislation.

Related Facts:
* The controversy highlighted the racial prejudices prevalent in the British legal system during colonial rule.
* This event acted as a catalyst for the formation of the **Indian National Congress** in 1885.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-038.q: The father of the Indian Renaissance was whom?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-038.explanation:
The correct answer is **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**. He is widely acclaimed as the **Father of the Indian Renaissance** and the **Maker of Modern India**.

His role in initiating social and educational reforms during the 19th century was transformative for Indian society. Key reasons for this title include:

*   **Social Reform:** He campaigned relentlessly against the **Sati** system, leading to its legal abolition in 1829.
*   **Religious Reform:** He founded the **Brahmo Samaj** in 1828 to promote monotheism and combat superstitious practices within Hinduism.
*   **Educational Reform:** He was a strong advocate for **Western education** and scientific thinking, believing it was essential for the progress of the Indian people.
*   **Journalism:** He pioneered Indian journalism by publishing newspapers in both Persian and Bengali to spread awareness on political and social issues.

Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore were monumental figures in India's freedom struggle and intellectual history, but they represent a later era than the initial 19th-century reform movement. Ram Pandurang, often associated with the Prarthana Samaj, was a significant reformer but did not initiate the broader renaissance movement in the way Raja Ram Mohan Roy did.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-038.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-039.q: Who is known as the Grand old man of Indian Nationalism?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-039.explanation:
The correct answer is **Dadabhai Naoroji**. He is widely recognized as the **Grand Old Man of India** due to his pioneering role in the Indian freedom struggle and his long-standing commitment to public life.

**Dadabhai Naoroji** was a founding member of the **Indian National Congress** and served as its president on three separate occasions. He was also the first Indian to become a member of the **British Parliament**, where he worked tirelessly to represent Indian interests.

His most significant contribution was the **Drain Theory**, which he popularized in his seminal work, *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*. He methodically explained how the British colonial administration was economically draining India's wealth, providing a strong foundation for the nationalist movement.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** is primarily known as the **Father of the Indian Renaissance** for his pioneering work in social and religious reform.
* **W.C. Bonnerjee** (often spelled Banerjee) holds the distinction of being the first president of the **Indian National Congress** in 1885.
* **Mahatma Gandhi** is revered as the **Father of the Nation** for his leadership in the non-violent struggle for independence.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-040.q: In which year Rettai Malai Srinivasan autobiography, Jeeviya Saritha surukkam was published?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-040.explanation:
The correct year for the publication of **Rettai Malai Srinivasan's** autobiography, titled ***Jeeviya Saritha Surukkam***, is **1939**.

Here is why this work is significant:

*   **Rettai Malai Srinivasan**, affectionately known as **Dravida Mani**, was a pioneering social reformer and a champion of the depressed classes in Tamil Nadu.
*   The title ***Jeeviya Saritha Surukkam*** translates to "A Brief Summary of My Life."
*   It is considered one of the **earliest autobiographies** written in Tamil by a Dalit leader, providing invaluable insights into the social struggles of the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
*   He was a contemporary of **B.R. Ambedkar** and played a crucial role in the **Poona Pact** alongside him, representing the interests of the marginalized communities.

While the options provided include other years, historical records confirm the publication of his memoir took place in **1939**, serving as a testament to his lifelong dedication to equality and justice.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-041.q: Who was a forerunner of the Akali movement?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-041.explanation:
The correct answer is **Singh Sabha**.

The **Singh Sabha Movement**, which emerged in the late 19th century, acted as a vital precursor to the later **Akali movement**. It focused on reforming Sikhism by removing non-Sikh practices and promoting education and the preservation of Sikh identity.

This movement laid the organizational and ideological groundwork for the **Shiromani Akali Dal**. The dedicated efforts of the Singh Sabha in managing Gurdwaras and fostering a sense of community directly influenced the later struggles for control over sacred shrines.

*   **Singh Chadda**, **Singh Balwanth**, and **Singh Rishab** are not recognized as historical movements or formal forerunners to the Akali movement in this context.

Related Facts:
*   The first Singh Sabha was established in **Amritsar** in **1873**.
*   The movement was a response to the growing influence of Christian missionaries and the Arya Samaj.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-042.q: Who established Samarasa Vedha Sanmarka Sangam?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-042.explanation:
The correct answer is **Ramalinga Swamigal**, popularly known as **Vallalar**. He established the **Samarasa Vedha Sanmarka Sangam** in **1865** at Vadalur.

The primary objective of this movement was to promote **universal brotherhood**, social equality, and the path of **compassion** (*Jeeva Karunyam*). He emphasized that the service of living beings is the highest form of worship.

Later, he renamed the organization as **Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Satya Sangam**. He also established the **Sathya Gnana Sabha** (Hall of Wisdom) to spread his teachings and founded the **Dharma Salai** to provide free food to the poor, which continues to function to this day.

Regarding the other options:

* **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** founded the **Arya Samaj** in 1875 to promote Vedic values and oppose idolatry.
* **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** established the **Brahmo Samaj** in 1828, often referred to as the father of the Indian Renaissance.
* **Swami Vivekanandha** was the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and established the **Ramakrishna Mission** in 1897.

**Ramalinga Swamigal**, popularly known as **Vallalar**, established the **Samarasa Vedha Sanmarka Sangam** in the year **1865**. This organization aimed to promote universal brotherhood and spiritual harmony among all people, transcending caste, creed, and religious barriers.

He later renamed it to **Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Satya Sangam** in 1872 to emphasize the concept of pure truth and non-violence. His teachings focused on the path of **Arutperum Jothi** (the Great Grace Light).

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-044.q: Ramalinga Swamigal established a free feeding house at which place?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-044.explanation:
The correct answer is **Vadalur**.

**Ramalinga Adigalar**, also known as **Vallalar**, established the **Sathya Gnana Sabha** (Hall of True Wisdom) and the **Sathya Dharma Salai** (House of Eternal Charity) in **Vadalur**.

The **Sathya Dharma Salai** was founded in **1867** with the primary objective of providing free food to the poor and hungry without any discrimination based on caste or creed. This practice of feeding the hungry, known as **"Oru Me Unavu"**, remains a central part of the philosophy he propagated, which he called **"Arutperunjothi Vallalar"** or the way of universal compassion.

While Ramalinga Swamigal spent his childhood in **Chidambaram** and later lived in **Karunguzhi**, it was specifically in **Vadalur** that he institutionalized his humanitarian services. The site continues to be a major pilgrimage center today, particularly during the **Thai Poosam** festival.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-045.q: Ramalinga Swamigal songs was published under the title of __________
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-045.explanation:
The correct title for the collection of songs composed by **Ramalinga Swamigal** (also known as **Vallalar**) is **Thiruvarutpa**.

The term **Thiruvarutpa** translates to "Songs of Divine Grace." It consists of six distinct parts known as *Thirumurais*.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Arutpa** is sometimes used as a shorthand, but **Thiruvarutpa** is the formal and complete title of the work.
* **Marutpa** is a term famously used by his contemporary critics to disparage his works, claiming they were not divinely inspired. **Vallalar** successfully defended his work against these allegations, solidifying the name **Thiruvarutpa**.

**Ramalinga Swamigal** founded the **Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sathya Sangam**, which emphasizes compassion, universal brotherhood, and the worship of light (*Jyoti*). His teachings and poetry continue to be a significant part of Tamil spiritual literature.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-046.q: What is the real name of Vaikunda Swamigal?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-046.explanation:
The real name of **Vaikunda Swamigal**, the prominent social reformer and founder of the **Ayyavazhi** sect, was **Mudichudum Perumal**.

He was born in **Swamithope** in the Kanyakumari district. His parents originally named him **Mudichudum Perumal**, which translates to "the king who wears the crown."

The local authorities at the time objected to this name, as it was perceived to imply royal status. Consequently, he was forced to change his name to **Muthukutty**.

He is widely revered for his socio-religious movement that challenged the caste system and fought for equality in **Travancore**. His teachings are compiled in the holy book known as the **Akilathirattu Ammanai**.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-047.q: Who criticised the rule of the British and the rule of the Rajah of Travancore as the rule of white devils and black devils respectively?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-047.explanation:
The correct answer is **Vaikunda Swamigal**.

**Vaikunda Swamigal** was a prominent social reformer in the 19th century who founded the **Ayyavazhi** sect. He was a staunch critic of both the prevailing social hierarchy and colonial governance.

He famously described the British rule as **"White Devils"** (*Ven-nees*) and the rule of the Travancore Maharajas as **"Black Devils"** (*Kar-nees*). This critique highlighted his opposition to both foreign imperialism and the oppressive local feudal system.

His teachings focused on **equality**, social justice, and the upliftment of the downtrodden. By calling out both powers, he voiced the struggles of the marginalized communities who suffered under the dual pressure of British taxation and the caste-based discrimination practiced by the Princely State of Travancore.

**Vaikunda Swamigal**'s movement played a significant role in fostering self-respect and social consciousness among the people of southern Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-048.explanation:
The term **Thiruvarutpa** is a compilation of the devotional poems composed by the revered Tamil saint **Ramalinga Adigalar**, popularly known as **Vallalar**.

To understand the meaning, we break down the word into its Tamil roots:
*   **Thiru**: Means holy, sacred, or divine.
*   **Arul**: Means grace or divine compassion.
*   **Pa**: Means songs or verses.

Therefore, **Thiruvarutpa** translates directly to **Songs of Grace**.

This collection reflects the saint's philosophy of **Suddha Sanmarga**, which emphasizes universal love, compassion, and the pursuit of truth. It is considered one of the most significant literary and spiritual works in the Tamil language.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-050.q: In the year 1882, John Rathinam and Iyothee thasser established a movement called __________
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-050.explanation:
The correct answer is **Dravida Kazhagam**.

In 1882, **Pandithar Iyothee Thassar** and **John Rathinam** jointly established an organization called **Dravida Kazhagam** (Dravidian Association). This movement was pioneered to fight for the socio-economic development, education, and civil rights of the marginalized and oppressed classes in Tamil Nadu.

Following this, in 1885, they launched a weekly journal named **Dravida Pandiyan** to expose the injustices faced by the downtrodden and to propagate their reformist ideas. Iyothee Thassar later went on to establish the **Dravida Mahajana Sabha** in 1891, organizing its first conference in Ooty.

As for the other options, **Dravida Pandiyan** was a magazine started in 1885, not the 1882 movement. **Dravida Mahajana Sabha** was founded by Iyothee Thassar later in 1891. Lastly, **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam** (DMK) was a political party founded much later in 1949 by C. N. Annadurai.

The correct answer is **Kudiyarasu**.

The **Self-Respect Movement**, founded by **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy** in 1925, sought to promote rationalism and social equality in Tamil society. To propagate these radical ideas, Periyar launched the journal **Kudiyarasu** (meaning "Republic" or "People's Government") in the same year.

**Kudiyarasu** served as the official mouthpiece for the movement, consistently advocating for the abolition of the caste system, the empowerment of women, and the removal of superstitious practices. It became a powerful tool for political and social awakening in the Tamil-speaking regions.

Regarding the other options provided:

* **Swadesamitran** was a prominent nationalist newspaper started by **G. Subramania Iyer**. It was the first Tamil daily newspaper and played a vital role in the Indian Independence movement, but it was not the organ of the Self-Respect Movement.
* **Swachh** is not a historical newspaper associated with this movement.
* **Gnana Banu** was a literary magazine edited by **Subramania Bharati**, focusing on literature and nationalist thoughts rather than the specific social reform agenda of Periyar.

Therefore, **Kudiyarasu** remains the historical and ideological pillar of the Self-Respect Movement.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-056.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-057.q: The aspect of the caste system which was particularly condemned by all social reformers was __________
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-057.explanation:
The correct answer is **Untouchability**.

While the Varna and Jati systems formed the structural foundation of the caste hierarchy, **Untouchability** was the specific, dehumanizing practice that social reformers across all eras targeted for total eradication. It represented the most severe form of social exclusion and violation of human dignity.

Here is why it stands out:

*   **Human Rights:** Reformers like **Mahatma Gandhi**, **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, and **Jyotirao Phule** viewed untouchability as a "blot on humanity" and a fundamental moral failure of society.
*   **Legal Action:** Because of this universal condemnation, the practice was explicitly abolished under **Article 17** of the Indian Constitution, which makes the enforcement of any disability arising out of "untouchability" a punishable offense.
*   **Distinction:** The Varna system refers to the theoretical four-fold division of society, while Jati refers to specific birth-based occupational groups. While reformers criticized the rigidity of these systems, untouchability was the specific social atrocity that demanded immediate legal and social intervention.

By focusing on the elimination of untouchability, reformers aimed to dismantle the most oppressive manifestation of the caste hierarchy, ensuring equal access to public places, education, and social participation for all.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-057.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-058.q: The Madras Native Association was formed on
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-058.explanation:
The **Madras Native Association** (MNA) was the first political organization in the Madras Presidency to articulate the grievances of the people against the policies of the **British East India Company**. It was officially founded on **26 February 1852**.

The organization was established primarily through the efforts of **Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty**, a prominent merchant and social reformer. He is often remembered for his dedication to exposing the plight of the peasantry and the abuses of the colonial administration.

Key points to remember about the MNA:

*   It was formed to represent the interests of the local population to the British authorities.
*   The association played a crucial role in highlighting issues such as **police torture** and the **inequities of the land revenue system**.
*   Its primary publication, the newspaper **The Crescent**, served as a powerful voice to challenge the prevailing colonial narrative.
*   The MNA eventually merged into the **Madras Mahajana Sabha** in 1884, which paved the way for more organized nationalist politics in the region.

While other dates in February 1852 are often cited in various contexts, historical records confirm **26 February** as the formal inauguration date of this pioneering political body.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-058.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-059.q: The Vernacular press Act was passed in which year?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-059.explanation:
The correct answer is **1878**.

The **Vernacular Press Act** was enacted in **1878** during the viceroyalty of **Lord Lytton**. This law was designed to curtail the freedom of the Indian language press and prevent the expression of criticism against the British administration.

Key points to remember:

* The act was officially titled the **Vernacular Press Act (Act IX of 1878)**.
* It empowered the government to issue search warrants and inspect the content of vernacular newspapers before publication.
* It was famously referred to as the **"Gagging Act"** because it effectively stifled political dissent.
* The act remained in force for a few years until it was eventually repealed in **1882** by **Lord Ripon**, who is known for his more liberal policies toward Indian self-government.

The other options (1875, 1876, 1877) do not correspond to the year this legislation was passed. Understanding this act is crucial for the **TNPSC** syllabus as it highlights the colonial-era restrictions on Indian nationalism and the evolution of the freedom struggle.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-059.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-060.q: Who wrote the commentaries on the sangam texts, pattinappalai and mullaipattu?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-060.explanation:
The correct answer is **Maraimalai Adigal**.

**Maraimalai Adigal**, a renowned Tamil scholar and a pioneer of the **Pure Tamil Movement** (Thani Thamizh Iyakkam), contributed significantly to Tamil literature. He wrote insightful commentaries on these specific **Sangam** poems, helping readers understand the deep meaning of the ancient texts.

While the other figures listed are prominent leaders in Tamil history, they are not the authors of these specific commentaries:
* **Subramanya Bharathi** is celebrated for his revolutionary poetry and prose.
* **Parithimar Kalaignar** was a scholar who advocated for Tamil to be recognized as a classical language.
* **Thanthai Periyar** focused on social reform and the Self-Respect Movement.

Related Facts:
* **Maraimalai Adigal** is often called the father of the **Pure Tamil Movement**.
* **Pattinappalai** describes the port city of Poompuhar, while **Mullaipattu** focuses on the life of shepherds in the forest region.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-060.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-061.q: Who was one of the earliest reformers,influenced by the western ideas to initiate social reforms in India?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-061.explanation:
The correct answer is **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**. He is widely recognized as the **Father of Indian Renaissance** and the pioneer of modern Indian social reform.

He was the first to advocate for **western education** and scientific thinking to reform Indian society. His influence was instrumental in the abolition of **Sati** in 1829, which he fought against using both traditional scriptures and humanitarian logic.

In 1828, he founded the **Brahmo Samaj**, an organization that campaigned against caste discrimination, idolatry, and child marriage. His efforts paved the way for subsequent reformers in the 19th century.

*   **Mahatma Gandhi** was a leader of the 20th-century national movement, long after the initial wave of social reforms began.
*   **Rabindranath Tagore** was a prominent intellectual and poet, but he emerged much later in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
*   **Atmaram Pandurang** (often referred to in the context of Prarthana Samaj) was a reformer influenced by the work of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, rather than being the earliest initiator.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-061.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-062.q: In which year Brahmosamaj was founded?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-062.explanation:
The **Brahmo Samaj** was founded in the year **1828**.

It was established by the great social reformer **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in Kolkata. The organization was initially known as the **Brahmo Sabha**.

Its primary objective was to worship the eternal, unsearchable, and immutable **God** who is the creator and preserver of the universe. It played a pivotal role in the **Indian Renaissance** by advocating against social evils like **Sati** and promoting monotheism.

The other dates provided (1825, 1826, and 1827) do not mark the inception of this movement, making **1828** the historically accurate answer.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-062.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-063.explanation:
The **Brahmo Samaj** was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in **1828**.

He established it as a reformist movement within Hinduism to advocate for **monotheism** and the eradication of social evils like **Sati**. Initially called the **Brahmo Sabha**, it played a pivotal role in the **Indian Renaissance**.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **R.G. Bhandarkar** was a prominent social reformer associated with the **Prarthana Samaj** in Western India.
* **Ram Pandurang** (Atmaram Pandurang) was one of the founders of the **Prarthana Samaj** in 1867.
* **Tagore** (referring to Rabindranath Tagore) belonged to a later generation of the Brahmo movement; his father, **Debendranath Tagore**, was a key leader who revitalized the organization after Raja Ram Mohan Roy's death.

Raja Ram Mohan Roy is widely regarded as the **Father of Modern India** for his relentless efforts in modernizing Indian society and education.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-063.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-064.q: Who is the father of Rabindranath Tagore?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-064.explanation:
The father of **Rabindranath Tagore** is **Maharishi Debendranath Tagore**.

He was a prominent leader of the **Brahmo Samaj** and a significant figure in the **Bengal Renaissance**. He was given the title **Maharishi**, which means "great sage," due to his deep spiritual devotion and intellectual influence.

The other options are incorrect for the following reasons:

* **Ram Pandurang** was the father of Pandurang Sadashiv Sane, a famous Marathi writer.
* **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** was a social reformer and a close associate of the Tagore family, but he was not Rabindranath Tagore's father.
* **Maharishi Rabindranath Tagore** is incorrect as it assigns the title of the father to the son himself.

Rabindranath Tagore was born into the wealthy and intellectually vibrant **Jorasanko Tagore family** in Kolkata. His upbringing in this environment played a crucial role in shaping his future as a poet, philosopher, and the first non-European to win the **Nobel Prize in Literature**.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-064.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-065.q: In which year Prarthana Samaj was founded?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-065.explanation:
The **Prarthana Samaj** (Prayer Society) was founded in **Bombay** in the year **1867**. Therefore, the correct option is 1867, which corresponds to the third option provided in your list.

This socio-religious reform movement was established under the guidance of **Keshab Chandra Sen**, who visited Bombay that year to inspire local reformers.

The key figures behind its establishment were:
* **Atmaram Pandurang** (the first president)
* **Mahadev Govind Ranade**
* **R.G. Bhandarkar**

The primary objective of the **Prarthana Samaj** was to reform Hindu society by promoting monotheism, opposing the caste system, and advocating for the remarriage of widows and the education of women.

It was deeply influenced by the **Brahmo Samaj** of Bengal but functioned with a distinct focus on the social and religious traditions of Maharashtra. It sought to modernize society while staying grounded in the spiritual teachings of the Marathi saints like **Namdev**, **Tukaram**, and **Eknath**.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-065.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-066.q: Who is the Founder of Prarthana Samaj?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-066.explanation:
The correct answer is **Atmaram Pandurang**.

**Atmaram Pandurang** founded the **Prarthana Samaj** in 1867 in **Bombay**. He established this society to focus on social reform and religious reform within the context of **Hinduism**, promoting the worship of one God and rejecting the caste system.

*   **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** founded the **Brahmo Samaj** in 1828.
*   **R.C. Bhandarkar** was a prominent member who later contributed to the movement, but he did not found it.
*   **Tagore** refers to the family of **Rabindranath Tagore**, associated with the **Brahmo Samaj** movement in Bengal.

Related Facts:
*   The movement was inspired by the **Brahmo Samaj** of Bengal.
*   **Mahadev Govind Ranade** became the main driving force behind the organization after joining in 1870.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-066.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-067.q: Rajaram Mohan Roy established the Brahmo samaj at which place?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-067.explanation:
**Raja Ram Mohan Roy** established the **Brahmo Sabha** (later known as the **Brahmo Samaj**) in **Calcutta** on August 20, **1828**.

This organization was founded to promote **monotheism** and reform social practices within Hinduism. It played a significant role in the **Indian Renaissance** by advocating against social evils like **Sati**.

The other cities listed—Delhi, Mumbai, and Chennai—were important centers of socio-religious reform later on, but they were not the birthplace of the Brahmo Samaj.

Calcutta served as the intellectual hub for reformist movements during the **19th century** due to its status as the administrative center of the British East India Company.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-067.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-068.q: __________ is a reshaping or reforming of culturally accepted laws and norms in light of new cultural paradigms that occur over time
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-068.explanation:
The correct answer is **Social Action**.

**Social Action** refers to the deliberate process of collective efforts aimed at challenging, reshaping, or reforming existing social structures, laws, and cultural norms. It occurs when a group recognizes that current societal frameworks no longer align with emerging cultural paradigms or needs.

Here is why the other options do not fit:

* **Social Work** is primarily a professional practice focused on providing direct support, services, and interventions to individuals, families, and communities to improve their well-being.
* **Social Reforms** generally refer to the outcome or the movement of changing specific systemic issues, but **Social Action** specifically captures the proactive process of mobilizing people to enact these cultural and legal shifts.
* **Social Science** is the academic study of society and human relationships; it is the field of research rather than the act of changing societal norms.

In essence, **Social Action** serves as the dynamic engine that drives progress by transforming stagnant laws to better reflect the evolving values of a society. This concept is a core element in sociology and social advocacy studies within the **TNPSC** syllabus.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-068.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-069.q: __________ refused remarriage and fought for an education, becoming an educationist for 35 years during the British Raj
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-069.explanation:
The correct answer is **Ms. R. Lilavati**.

**R. Lilavati** was a courageous reformer who defied the traditional societal pressures of her time. After the death of her husband, she firmly refused to remarry and dedicated her entire life to the pursuit of knowledge and the upliftment of society.

She broke barriers by entering the field of education and served as an educationist for 35 years under the British Raj. Her tireless efforts paved the way for women's empowerment in education during a challenging era.

*   **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** was a pioneer who became the first woman legislator in India and campaigned against the Devadasi system.
*   **Dr. S. Dharmambai** is well known for her role in the anti-Hindi agitation and her work in promoting Tamil education.
*   **Ramabai Ranade** founded the Seva Sadan in Mumbai to provide social and educational support to women.

Related Facts:
*   Her dedication highlights the struggle for women's autonomy in 20th-century India.
*   She stands as a symbol of intellectual resistance against regressive customs.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-069.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-070.q:
Match : [Movement - Reformers]
A) Brahmo Samaj - 1) Natesan
B) SNDP - 2) E.V. Ramaswamy
C) Justice party - 3) Sri Narayana Guru
D) Self Respect movement - 4) Raja Ram Mohan Roy
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-070.explanation:
To solve this question, we must match each social reform movement with its founding leader or key proponent:

*   **Brahmo Samaj** was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in 1828 to promote monotheism and social reform in Bengal. This corresponds to **A-4**.

*   **SNDP** (Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam) was established by **Sri Narayana Guru** in Kerala to advocate for the rights and social upliftment of the Ezhava community. This corresponds to **B-3**.

*   **Justice Party** (South Indian Liberal Federation) was formed by leaders like **C. Natesan**, T.M. Nair, and P. Thyagaraya Chetty to secure representation for non-Brahmins. This corresponds to **C-1**.

*   **Self-Respect Movement** was launched by **E.V. Ramaswamy** (Periyar) in 1925 to promote rationalism and equality, emphasizing the removal of caste discrimination. This corresponds to **D-2**.

Matching these together, we get the sequence: **A-4, B-3, C-1, D-2**.

Therefore, the second option is the correct sequence.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-070.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-071.q:
Which of the following statements about Ayothidasa panditar is true?
i) He founded Adi Dravida Mahajana Shabha.
ii) He established the Sakya Buddhist Society.
iii) He joined servants of untouchables society.
iv) He published ‘One Paise Tamilan’ News Paper.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-071.explanation:
The correct answer is **(ii) and (iv)**.

**Ayothidasa Panditar** was a great social reformer who advocated for the rights of the depressed classes. He established the **Sakya Buddhist Society** in 1898 to promote the principles of Buddhism among the people.

He also started a weekly journal named **‘One Paise Tamilan’** (Oru Paisa Tamilan) in 1907. This newspaper became a powerful tool to spread his views on social justice and cultural identity.

Other options are incorrect because:
* He did not found the **Adi Dravida Mahajana Sabha** (which was founded by Rettamalai Srinivasan).
* He did not join the **Servants of Untouchables Society** (which was established by Mahatma Gandhi).

**Related Facts:**
* He emphasized that the people of the depressed classes were original Buddhists.
* The newspaper name was later changed simply to **‘Tamilan’**.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-071.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-072.q:
Match :

B) Suddhi Movement - 2) 1897
C) Ramakrishna Mission - 3) Madam Blavatsky

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-072.explanation:
To determine the correct matching, let us analyze each movement and its associated founder or year:

* **Theosophical Society**: Founded in 1875 by **Madam Blavatsky** and Henry Steel Olcott. Among the choices, **Madam Blavatsky** (3) is the correct match for A.

* **Suddhi Movement**: This movement was initiated by **Dayanand Saraswati** (founder of Arya Samaj) to reconvert those who had left Hinduism. Therefore, B matches with 4.

* **Samarasa Suddha Sanmarg**: Founded by **Ramalinga Swamigal** (Vallalar) in **1865** in Vadalur, Tamil Nadu. This matches D with 1.

Matching these findings:
A-3 (Theosophical Society - Madam Blavatsky)
B-4 (Suddhi Movement - Dayanand Saraswati)
C-2 (Ramakrishna Mission - 1897)
D-1 (Samarasa Suddha Sanmarg - 1865)

This corresponds to the sequence **A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1**, which is the first option.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-073.q: “Law and rules are only for the people, people are not for the law and the rules” said by
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-073.explanation:
The correct answer is **Kamarajar**.

**K. Kamarajar**, the former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu and a legendary leader, expressed this profound philosophy to emphasize that governance should serve the welfare of the public. He believed that the primary goal of any administration is to improve the lives of the common people rather than burdening them with rigid bureaucracy.

*   **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy** focused primarily on social reform and self-respect.
*   **Annadurai** championed the cause of state autonomy and Tamil identity.
*   **Rajaji** was known for his administrative acumen but held different ideological views on governance.

Related Facts:
*   Kamarajar is often called the 'Kingmaker' of Indian politics.
*   He is celebrated for introducing the **Mid-day Meal Scheme** in schools to increase attendance and reduce hunger.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-073.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-074.q: In Tamil Nadu the first ever celebration of May Day was organized in 1923 by
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-074.explanation:
The correct answer is **Singaravelar**.

**M. Singaravelar**, a prominent communist leader and freedom fighter, organized the first **May Day** celebration in India on **May 1, 1923**, in **Madras** (now Chennai).

He held two major meetings to mark this historic occasion:
1. One meeting was conducted at the **Madras High Court Beach**.
2. Another meeting was held at the **Triplicane Beach**.

This event was significant as it marked the beginning of organized **labor movements** in India. Singaravelar was a pioneer in advocating for the rights of workers and was the founder of the **Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan**.

He is often remembered as the father of the communist movement in South India, having been deeply influenced by the Russian Revolution. By organizing this event, he successfully integrated the Indian working class into the global movement for labor rights.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-074.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-075.q:
Pick out correct answer
i) Madras Mahajana Sabha - 1884
ii) South Indian People Association - 1919
iii) Non-Brahmin Manifesto - 1916
iv) Madras Literary Society - 1880
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-075.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4, as statements (i) and (iii) are historically accurate.

**Madras Mahajana Sabha** was established in **1884** by M. Veeraraghavachariar, P. Anandacharlu, and G. Subramaniam Iyer. It was one of the earliest nationalist organizations in the Madras Presidency, preceding the formation of the Indian National Congress.

The **Non-Brahmin Manifesto** was issued in **1916** by the **South Indian Liberal Federation** (commonly known as the Justice Party). It was drafted primarily by **P. Theagaraya Chetty** to highlight the grievances of non-Brahmins regarding their lack of representation in government jobs and education.

Regarding the incorrect statements:
* The **South Indian People Association** was actually founded in **1916**, not 1919. This association was the precursor to the Justice Party and served as the body responsible for publishing newspapers like *Justice*, *Dravidan*, and *Andhra Prakasika* to propagate non-Brahmin interests.
* The **Madras Literary Society** was established much earlier, in **1812**, to promote knowledge in science, literature, and the arts. It is one of the oldest institutions of its kind in India.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-075.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-076.q: Which among the following statements is true with the Self-Respect Movement?
options: Self-Respect Movement is a social protest against upper caste Hindus
Self-Respect movement was more interested in social freedom
Self-Respect movement directed its appeal mainly to land owning class
Self-Respect movement was initiated to win political independence
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-076.explanation:
**The correct answer is that the Self-Respect movement was more interested in social freedom.**

This movement, founded by **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy** in 1925, prioritized the **social dignity** and self-respect of the Dravidian people over political gains. It focused on challenging the oppressive caste hierarchy and societal norms that marginalized individuals.

The movement sought to liberate society from the clutches of caste-based discrimination, irrational beliefs, and gender inequality, firmly believing that social change is a prerequisite for any meaningful progress.

*   Option 1 is incorrect because it was a movement for equality rather than just a protest against a specific group.
*   Option 3 is incorrect as it appealed to all sections of the oppressed society, not just landowners.
*   Option 4 is incorrect because the primary goal was social reform, not political independence from colonial rule.

**Related Facts:**
*   The movement is also known as the **Dravidian Movement**.
*   It emphasized the importance of **rationalism** and self-reliance.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-076.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-077.q: Dr. Muthulakshmi fought against social evil?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-077.explanation:
**Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** is a historic figure in social reform, primarily known for her dedicated campaign against the **Devadasi system**.

While she advocated for the overall welfare of women and children, her most significant legislative achievement was the abolition of the **Devadasi system** in the Madras Presidency. She introduced the **Devadasi Abolition Bill** in the Madras Legislative Council, which eventually led to the end of this exploitative practice.

Here is why the other options do not fit this specific context:

* **Child marriage:** While she supported the **Child Marriage Restraint Act (Sarda Act)**, it was not her primary or singular focus compared to the Devadasi struggle.
* **Dowry system:** This became a major legal focus in India much later, primarily through the **Dowry Prohibition Act of 1961**.
* **Polygamy:** Although many social reformers of her time criticized this, Dr. Muthulakshmi is most famously remembered for her specific crusade against the institutionalized practice of Devadasi.

As a pioneer, she was also the first woman legislator in the Madras Legislative Council and the first woman doctor in India to graduate from the Madras Medical College. Her lifelong commitment to public health led her to establish the **Adyar Cancer Institute** in 1954, which remains one of the leading cancer treatment centers in India today.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-077.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-078.q: Revolutionary movements are mainly based on
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-078.explanation:
A **revolutionary movement** is defined by its intent to create a fundamental and rapid transformation of an existing social, political, or economic system. Unlike reformist movements, which seek small adjustments, revolutions aim for a total overhaul.

The core objective is the **reorganization of society**. This involves dismantling current institutions and replacing them with a new structure, hierarchy, or set of ideologies that alter the entire fabric of life.

Here is why the other options do not fit:

*   **Modification** refers to incremental changes, which is the hallmark of reform rather than revolution.
*   **Development** implies a gradual process of growth or improvement, which is not the primary goal of a radical revolution.
*   **Post-modern society** describes a specific historical or cultural period rather than the foundational objective of a revolutionary movement.

In essence, a revolution seeks to replace the existing order entirely. By changing the core principles of governance and social interaction, it achieves the complete **reorganization** of the social structure.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-078.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-079.q: Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam was established by
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-079.explanation:
The correct answer is **Ramalinga Adigal**, also widely known as **Vallalar**.

**Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam** was established by him in **1865** to promote the philosophy of universal brotherhood and service to humanity.

Key details about the organization:
*   It emphasizes the motto **"Service to living beings is the path to liberation."**
*   He advocated for a society free of caste, religious, and class divisions.
*   He founded the **Sathya Gnana Sabha** (Hall of True Wisdom) in **Vadalur** to practice this philosophy.

Regarding the other options:
*   **Chattambi Swamigal** and **Narayana Guru** were prominent social reformers in Kerala who worked against the caste system and for the upliftment of the oppressed.
*   **Ramana Maharishi** was a famous sage from Thiruvannamalai known for his teachings on **Self-enquiry** (Atma Vichara).

The confusion often arises because all these figures were great spiritual leaders in South India, but the specific establishment of the **Sanmarga Sangam** is uniquely attributed to **Ramalinga Adigal**.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-080.q:
The achievement of self respect movement was
1) Widow remarriage
2) Abolition of untouchability
3) Communal representation
4) Decline the influence of Varna Ghrama Dharma
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-080.explanation:
The correct answer is **All are correct**. The **Self-Respect Movement**, founded by **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy**, aimed to create a society where everyone lived with dignity and equal rights.

*   **Widow Remarriage**: Periyar strongly advocated for the rights of women, including the right for widows to remarry, to break social taboos.
*   **Abolition of untouchability**: The movement worked tirelessly to eliminate the caste-based discrimination and the practice of untouchability.
*   **Communal representation**: Periyar championed the cause of proportional representation to ensure social justice and equal opportunities for all communities in education and government jobs.
*   **Decline the influence of Varna Ashrama Dharma**: A primary goal of the movement was to dismantle the rigid hierarchy of the **Varna Ashrama Dharma** and the Brahminical hegemony that perpetuated inequality.

Related Facts:
*   The movement was officially launched in **1925**.
*   It emphasized **rationalism** and **self-respect** over religious dogma.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-080.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-081.q:
Which of the means adopted under self-respect movement
i) Violent protests against upper classes
ii) Undermine position of Brahmin priests by formalizing weddings without them
iii) Boycott of temples and places of Brahmin residence
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-081.explanation:
The correct answer is **Only (ii)**. The **Self-Respect Movement**, founded by **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy**, primarily focused on promoting rationalism, self-respect, and social equality among non-Brahmins.

Statement (ii) is correct because the movement advocated for **'Self-Respect Marriages'** (Suyamariyathai Thirumanam), which were conducted without Brahmin priests and religious rituals to challenge the traditional hierarchy. This was a symbolic way to restore dignity to the oppressed.

Statements (i) and (iii) are incorrect because the movement was firmly rooted in **non-violent, rationalistic persuasion** rather than violent protests. While it aimed to challenge caste hegemony, it did not endorse a blanket boycott of temples or residential areas as a core method of the movement's policy.

Related Facts:
* The movement was launched in **1925**.
* It prioritized the eradication of **caste-based discrimination** and the empowerment of women.
* The movement eventually merged with the **Justice Party** to form the **Dravidar Kazhagam** in **1944**.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-081.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-082.q:
Match : [Social Reform Reformers]
A) Abolition of Sati - 1) Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar
B) Temple Entry for Dalits - 2) Thanthai Periyar
C) Widow Remarriage Act - 3) Raja Ram Mohan Roy
D) Self respect movement against untouchability - 4) Ambedkar
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-082.explanation:
The correct match is **A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2**. Here is the breakdown of the reformers and their major contributions:

*   **Abolition of Sati (A-3):** **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** is known as the "Father of Modern India." He campaigned extensively against the practice of **Sati**, leading to its legal abolition by Lord William Bentinck in **1829**.

*   **Temple Entry for Dalits (B-4):** **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** was the primary leader who fought for the rights of the depressed classes. He led the famous **Kalaram Temple Entry Movement** in 1930 to demand equal access to temples for Dalits.

*   **Widow Remarriage Act (C-1):** **Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar** was a dedicated social reformer who fought for the rights of widows. His persistent efforts led to the passage of the **Hindu Widow Remarriage Act** in **1856**.

*   **Self-Respect Movement (D-2):** **Thanthai Periyar** (E.V. Ramasamy) launched the **Self-Respect Movement** in 1925. A core objective of this movement was to eradicate **untouchability**, promote social equality, and challenge the caste-based hierarchy in society.

By matching these historical contributions correctly, we arrive at the sequence **A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2**.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-082.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-083.q: India’s first organised Trade union was
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-083.explanation:
The correct answer is **Madras Labour Union**.

The **Madras Labour Union** was established in **1918** by **B.P. Wadia** along with **Thiru. V. Kalyanasundaram** (Thiru. Vi. Ka.). It is widely recognized by historians as the first registered and systematically organized trade union in India.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

*   **Madras Mahajana Sabha** was established in **1884** as a political organization aimed at promoting nationalist interests, not as a labor union.
*   **All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC)** was founded in **1920** to provide a national platform for workers. While it became the premier central organization, it was formed two years after the Madras Labour Union.
*   **South Indian Liberal Federation**, also known as the **Justice Party**, was a political party formed in **1916** to represent the interests of non-Brahmins in the Madras Presidency, not a labor union.

The formation of the **Madras Labour Union** marked a significant turning point in the Indian labor movement, as it introduced the concept of collective bargaining and formal structure to the struggle of industrial workers.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-083.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-084.q:
Which of the following organizations were established by Vadallur Vallalar?
a) Suddhasanmarga Sangam
b) Samathuva Samajam
c) Sathya Dharmashala
d) Sathya Gnanasabha
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-084.explanation:
The correct options are **a, c and d**. **Ramalinga Adigal**, popularly known as **Vallalar**, founded these institutions in **Vadalur** to promote his humanitarian philosophy known as **Sanmarga**.

* **Suddhasanmarga Sangam**: Established in 1865 to spread the philosophy of universal brotherhood.
* **Sathya Dharmashala**: Founded in 1867 to provide free food (*dharmashala*) to the hungry and poor, regardless of caste or religion.
* **Sathya Gnanasabha**: Established in 1872 as a place of spiritual light and worship, focusing on the concept of 'Arutperunjothi'.

Option **b** is incorrect because **Samathuva Samajam** was founded by **Ayothidasar**, a prominent social reformer, not by Vallalar.

Related Facts:
* Vallalar's famous collection of poems is known as **Thiruvarutpa**.
* He emphasized that 'Service to living beings is service to God'.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-086.q:
Which of the following statements are true in respect of Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy?
1) She was the first woman in India to get a degree in medicine.
2) She was the first woman Legislator in British India.
3) She was the first female student to be admitted in Maharaja's college.
4) She was the first woman to the legislative council.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-086.explanation:
The correct answer is **2, 3, and 4**. Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy was a visionary pioneer whose contributions shaped history.

She achieved the following milestones:
* She became the **first female student** to be admitted to the **Maharaja's College** in Pudukkottai, challenging gender norms of the time.
* She served as the **first woman legislator** in the Madras Legislative Council, becoming the first woman to hold such a position in British India.

While statement 1 suggests she was the first woman in India to receive a medical degree, this honor belongs to **Kadambini Ganguly** and **Anandibai Joshi**. Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy was, however, the **first woman to graduate in medicine from Madras Medical College**.

Related Facts:
* She founded the **Adyar Cancer Institute** in 1954.
* She was instrumental in the passage of the **Devadasi Abolition Act**.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-086.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-087.q:
Which of the following statements are true about Ramalinga Adigal?
1) He started the Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Satya Sangam in 1865.
2) He was against the caste system.
3) He established Satya Dharma Salai in 1867.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-087.explanation:
The correct answer is **option 3**. All three statements provided are true regarding the life and contributions of **Ramalinga Adigal**, also known as **Vallalar**.

**Ramalinga Adigal** was a prominent Tamil saint and philosopher. His contributions are as follows:

*   He founded the **Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Satya Sangam** in **1865**. This organization aimed to promote a universal path of spiritual truth, unity, and brotherhood, transcending religious and social barriers.
*   He was a staunch advocate for **social equality** and was firmly **against the caste system**. He believed that all human beings are equal and emphasized the path of mercy and compassion (*Jeeva Karunyam*) as the true essence of spiritual life.
*   In **1867**, he established the **Satya Dharma Salai** at **Vadalur**. This institution was created with the noble objective of providing free food to the poor and hungry, regardless of their background, reflecting his philosophy that "feeding the hungry is the highest form of worship."

Because all three statements accurately reflect the historical records of his social reforms and humanitarian initiatives, all are correct.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-088.q:
Which of the following are correctly paired?
1)  Nizhal Thaankalgal - Vaigunda Swamigal
2) Hindu Progressive Improvement Society - Rajaram Mohan Roy
3) Samarasa Sanmarka Sangam - Vallalar
4) Respect Morality - Vedanayagam Pillai
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-088.explanation:
The correct answer is **1 and 3**.

**Nizhal Thaankalgal** were established by **Ayya Vaikunda Swamigal** as places of worship and shelters for the downtrodden, promoting his philosophy of social equality. **Samarasa Suddha Sanmarka Sangam** was founded by **Ramalinga Adigal** (Vallalar) in 1865 to foster universal brotherhood and compassion, known as *Arutpa*.

Regarding the other options:
* **Hindu Progressive Improvement Society** was founded by **Pandithar Ayothee Thassar**, not Rajaram Mohan Roy.
* **Respect Morality** (Nithinerischool) is a collection of moral poems authored by **Kumaraguruparar**, not Vedanayagam Pillai.

Related Facts:
* Vallalar also established the **Sathya Dharma Salai** in Vadalur to provide free food to the needy.
* Vaikunda Swamigal's movement is also known as the **Ayya Vazhi** path.
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-088.topic: Impact of Social Reform Movements in the Socio-Economic Development of Tamil Nadu

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-089.q: The Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam was founded by
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-089.explanation:
The correct answer is **Ramalinga Adigal**, also known as **Vallalar**.

**Ramalinga Swamigal** founded the **Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam** in **1865**. His philosophy focused on the concept of **"Jeeva Karunya"** (compassion for all living beings) and the unity of all humanity.

The movement emphasized:
* Abolition of caste and religious distinctions.
* The importance of charity and feeding the hungry, which led him to establish the **Sathya Dharma Salai** at Vadalur.
* The promotion of universal brotherhood and love through his central motto, **"Arutperunjothi"** (Supreme Grace Light).

The other options are associated with different social and political movements in Tamil Nadu:
* **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** was a pioneer in healthcare and a fierce advocate for the abolition of the Devadasi system.
* **T.M. Nair** was one of the founding leaders of the **Justice Party**, which advocated for the rights of non-Brahmins.
* **Thanthai Periyar** (E.V. Ramasamy) is the father of the **Self-Respect Movement**, which focused on rationalism and social equality.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-090.q: Which among the following was the first Christian Ashram established in the South?
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-090.explanation:
The correct answer is **Christukula Ashram at Tiruppatur**.

It is important to note that the **Christukula Ashram** was founded in **1921** by two medical missionaries, **Dr. Paton** and **Dr. Jesudasan**, in the town of Tiruppatur. This institution is historically recognized as the first **Christian Ashram** established in India, blending Indian ascetic traditions with Christian spiritual practices.

While the other options mention various religious centers, they do not hold the historical distinction of being the first Christian Ashram in the South.

The **Christukula Ashram** (which translates to "Family of Christ") became a model for later ashrams across the country. It focused on **inter-religious dialogue**, **holistic healing**, and **rural service**, making it a pioneer in the history of Indian Christianity.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-091.q: “The temple entry Authorisation and Indemnity Act” was passed in
questions/tn-econ-trend-135-091.explanation:
The correct answer is **1939**.

The **Madras Temple Entry Authorisation and Indemnity Act** was passed by the government led by **C. Rajagopalachari** in the Madras Presidency.

This legislation was a significant milestone in the social reform movement in Tamil Nadu. Its primary purposes were:

*   To grant legal permission for the entry of all castes into Hindu temples.
*   To provide legal protection (indemnity) to temple authorities and trustees who allowed lower-caste individuals to enter and worship in temples.

This act was part of the broader efforts to address the social exclusion faced by **Dalits** and other marginalized communities, championed by the Indian National Congress during its time in provincial government.

While the declared option provided in your prompt is 1940 (index 2), the act actually received the Governor-General's assent and was officially enacted in **1939**.

Regarding the other statements, her advocacy focused on raising the marriage age, but the specific legal recommendations and the details regarding the **Padma Vibhushan** award are inaccurate in this context. While she received the **Padma Bhushan** in 1956, she was not awarded the Padma Vibhushan.

Reason [R] : The Bill which later became the Devadasi Abolition Act, declared the “Pottukattu Ceremony” Illegal.

questions/tn-econ-trend-135-096.explanation:
The correct option is **3**. Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

**Muthulakshmi Ammaiyar**, a pioneering social reformer, introduced the bill in the **Madras Legislative Council** in **1930** with the goal of abolishing the **Devadasi system**.

The first general election in India took place between 1951 and 1952 to constitute the first **Lok Sabha**.

Out of the 489 seats contested in this historic election, a total of **22 women** were successfully elected as members of the lower house.

* **33** is often associated with the reservation quota debates but does not reflect the 1952 outcome.
* **2** is significantly lower than the actual number of women who participated and won.
* **222** is an inaccurately high figure, as it far exceeds the total number of female candidates who even stood for election at that time.

These 22 women pioneers played a crucial role in shaping the early legislative processes of independent India. This election marked a significant milestone for **gender representation** in Indian democracy, as it allowed women to exercise their right to vote and hold office for the first time on such a massive national scale.

It effectively functioned as a forum for social reform and political discourse.

Regarding the second statement, the movement's core objective was the total eradication of the caste system, the removal of superstitions, and the achievement of social equality. options: Separate dining for Brahmin and Non - Brahmin students in congress sponsored schools
Having a quarrel with V.V.S. Iyer
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-005.explanation:
**E.V. Ramasamy Periyar** was a prominent leader in the **Tamil Nadu Congress Committee** during the early 1920s. His departure from the party was driven by his growing disillusionment with the leadership's stance on social discrimination.

The primary catalyst for his exit was the incident at the **Cheranmadevi Gurukulam**. This institution was established by **V.V.S. Iyer** and was funded by the Congress party.

Periyar discovered that the school practiced **caste-based discrimination**, specifically by maintaining **separate dining halls** for Brahmin and non-Brahmin students.

As a staunch advocate for social equality and the **Self-Respect Movement**, Periyar demanded that these discriminatory practices be abolished. He insisted that the Congress party should not provide financial support to institutions that promoted caste segregation.

When the Congress leadership, particularly **C. Rajagopalachari**, refused to condemn or take decisive action against this practice, Periyar realized that the party was not committed to eradicating the **caste system**.

Consequently, Periyar resigned from the Congress party in **1925**. This event marked a turning point in his political career, leading him to focus entirely on his **Self-Respect Movement** and the struggle for the dignity of non-Brahmins.
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-005.topic: Political Parties and Welfare Schemes for Various Sections of People

questions/tn-econ-trend-136-006.q: __________ was India’s first woman Governor, a Political Activist, member of the Indian National Congress and a poet
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-006.explanation:
The correct answer is **Sarojini Naidu**.

**Sarojini Naidu** was appointed as the Governor of the United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh) in 1947. This historic appointment made her the **first woman to hold the office of Governor** in any Indian state after independence.

Often referred to as the **Nightingale of India** (*Bharat Kokila*) for her literary contributions, she was a renowned poet whose works include *The Golden Threshold* and *The Bird of Time*. She played a pivotal role in the Indian freedom struggle as a prominent leader of the **Indian National Congress**.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Vijayalakshmi Pandit** was a prominent diplomat and the first woman to be elected President of the United Nations General Assembly, but she was not the first woman Governor.
* **Muthulakshmi Reddy** was a distinguished physician and the first woman legislator in British India, known for her social work and the establishment of the Adyar Cancer Institute.
* **Annie Besant** was a British socialist, theosophist, and a key figure in the Indian Home Rule movement who served as the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1917, but she never served as a Governor.
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-006.topic: Political Parties and Welfare Schemes for Various Sections of People

questions/tn-econ-trend-136-007.q: First Municipal Corporation in India was set up at
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-007.explanation:
The first Municipal Corporation in India was established in **Madras** (now Chennai) in the year **1688**.

This historical development was initiated by the **British East India Company** to improve local administration and revenue collection. The corporation was established under a Royal Charter issued by **King James II**.

Here is why the other options are incorrect in this context:

*   **Bombay** and **Calcutta** followed later. Bombay established its municipal corporation in 1793, while Calcutta's municipal governance was structured shortly thereafter.
*   **Delhi** became a major center for municipal administration much later, especially after it became the capital of British India in 1911.

It is interesting to note that the **Madras Municipal Corporation** is not only the oldest in India but also one of the oldest in the world outside of Great Britain. This system eventually paved the way for the modern urban governance structure seen in India today under the **74th Constitutional Amendment Act**.
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-007.topic: Political Parties and Welfare Schemes for Various Sections of People

questions/tn-econ-trend-136-008.q: “Hindu Marriages (Tamil Nadu) Amendment Bill” was introduced in the year 1967 by
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-008.explanation:
The correct answer is **C.N. Annadurai**.

In **1967**, after the **DMK** party came to power, the government led by Chief Minister **C.N. Annadurai** introduced the **Hindu Marriages (Tamil Nadu) Amendment Bill**.

This landmark legislation was aimed at providing legal recognition to **Self-Respect Marriages** (*Suyamariyathai Thirumanam*). These are marriages performed without a **Brahmin priest** and without traditional Vedic rituals, emphasizing the principles of the **Self-Respect Movement** founded by **Periyar E.V. Ramasamy**.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Rajaji** was a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress and served as Chief Minister much earlier, focusing on different socio-economic reforms.
* **Kumarasamy Raja** served as the Chief Minister of the Madras Presidency between 1949 and 1952.
* **Kamarajar** was a stalwart of the Congress party who served as Chief Minister from 1954 to 1963, known primarily for his contributions to education and the mid-day meal scheme.

The legalizing of **Self-Respect Marriages** is considered a major milestone in the history of **Dravidian politics**, as it upheld the right of individuals to marry based on equality and rationalist values rather than caste-based traditions.
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-008.topic: Political Parties and Welfare Schemes for Various Sections of People

questions/tn-econ-trend-136-009.q: During the 1962 election, in which constituency Anna was defeated?
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-009.explanation:
In the **1962 Madras Legislative Assembly election**, C.N. Annadurai, the founder of the **DMK**, contested from the **Kanchipuram** constituency.

He faced a defeat against the Congress candidate, **P. Srinivasan**, by a margin of 1,666 votes.

Here is why the other options are incorrect:

* **Chennai**: Anna did not contest from a Chennai constituency during the 1962 Assembly elections.
* **Salem**: Anna was not a candidate in Salem during this specific election.
* **Nagercoil**: This constituency is located in the Kanyakumari district, and it was not the site of his 1962 contest.

Despite this defeat, the DMK party gained significant ground in the 1962 elections, setting the stage for their eventual victory in 1967. Following his defeat, Anna served as a member of the **Rajya Sabha**, where he became known for his powerful speeches on issues like the **Official Languages Act**.

questions/tn-econ-trend-136-010.q:
Match the political parties with their founding years
A) Indian National Congress - 1) 2013
B) All india Trinamool congress - 2) 1925
C) National People’s Party - 3) 1885
D) Communist Party of india (CPI) - 4) 1998
questions/tn-econ-trend-136-010.explanation:
The correct matching for the political parties and their respective founding years is as follows:

*   **Indian National Congress (INC)** was founded on December 28, **1885**. This makes A-3.
*   **All India Trinamool Congress (AITC)** was founded by Mamata Banerjee on January 1, **1998**. This makes B-4.
*   **National People’s Party (NPP)** was founded by P. A. Sangma on January 6, **2013**. This makes C-1.
*   **Communist Party of India (CPI)** was founded on December 26, **1925** in Kanpur. This makes D-2.

By connecting these facts, we arrive at the sequence: **A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2**.

Comparing this to the provided options, this corresponds to **Option 2**.

**Quick Study Tips:**
*   The **INC** is the oldest major political party in India, established during the British Raj.
*   The **CPI** represents one of the oldest communist movements, founded shortly after the global influence of the Russian Revolution.
*   The **NPP** is significant for being the first political party from the North-East to achieve the status of a National Party.
